objects.description: Covers name and filename mismatch, an empty description, an unknown front-matter key, missing front matter, and a block token used inline.

objects.title: A declared provider hook captures the person's raw prompts below the model, and doctor proves it by running it
objects.description: Covers the five states a provider can be in, idempotence on the provider's prompt identity, an archive that is ignored and untracked, a record set that cannot carry model output, the record-and-rendering pair every prompt is kept as, and the schema identifier resolving to the two files that describe both halves.

objects.title: A captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or records that none could be resolved; the archive is private, bounded and free of credential material
objects.description: The mapping from a provider session to an episode used to exist only while the episode was open, so a closed episode's prompts became unattributable at once — 713 of this repository's 974 records. The record now carries the episode, the provider session, the repository and the worktree, with the provenance of the link; the archive is 0600 and bounded by prompts.retention_max_days and prompts.retention_max_bytes, which prune the body and keep the record; and credential shapes are replaced before anything is persisted. The unlinked legacy records stay unlinked: the evidence for them does not exist, and this claim does not pretend otherwise.

objects.title: The provider bootstraps the policy declares (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, ...) are a target of majordomus generate, rendered from the policy and the provider templates byte for byte as the shell tool renders them, and generate --check refuses a hand-edited or stale one in CI
objects.description: One renderer, two entry points that agree on every stamp; the policy is the only input (its hash and the profiles' is the stamp's first hash). A target outside the repository, a provider without a template, a token the policy cannot fill, and an always_loaded target over the budget are refused with the reason, and nothing is written. Region mode keeps the host document outside the markers. apps/majordomus-cli/tests/providers_projection.rs covers the fixture side; CI runs generate --check on every push.

objects.title: The right prior record is resolved by worktree and branch, and an unrelated one is never offered
objects.description: Same worktree and branch, else same branch, else nothing. Ties within one second are broken by ledger order. Absence is reported as absence.

objects.title: Rotating the ledger archives the oldest lines and never deletes them
objects.description: Refuses to overwrite an existing archive, and does nothing when the ledger is under its cap.

objects.title: Durable records are searchable literally, across kinds, without an index
objects.description: A fixed-string grep in authority order. No ranking, no embedding, no index that could fall out of step with the records it describes.

objects.title: A projection can own only the region between its markers, leaving the rest of the file untouched
objects.description: How a repository that already has a hand-written CLAUDE.md adopts Majordomus. An edit outside the markers is never drift; an edit inside them is caught. Malformed markers are refused, not guessed at.

objects.title: A release archive carries every path once and carries nothing but files and directories
objects.description: The packer reads back what it wrote and deletes an archive carrying a repeated path or an entry that is not a file or a directory; the verifier checks the same two properties again on the runner that built it. There is no fallback packer, because an archive packed another way is not the one that was verified.

objects.title: A release publishes an artifact for every supported target or it is not published
objects.description: The build matrix stops at the first failure, publication begins only when every build succeeded, and the recorder refuses to write a record missing a target the model marks supported.

objects.title: Every finding carries the command that reproduces it
The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked
The roadmap is derived from milestone state, and no document may be a second authority for it
objects.description: The sequence is the topological rank of the milestone graph, so no list of versions exists anywhere. While a hand-written roadmap table survives, the doctrine holds it to the model in both directions; once it is gone the check holds trivially, which is the regression it exists to refuse.

objects.title: Routing recommendations will be derived from measured cost and outcome data
objects.description: Recommendations only. Majordomus does not invoke a model.

objects.title: A rule that no program can express says so in its own front matter, with the reason, and is counted apart from every rule that has a gate
objects.description: Some rules genuinely have no machine expression: the provenance of what was written, whether a mechanism earns its cost. Before `reviewed_because` those sat in a debt list beside rules that merely had not been got round to, and the two were indistinguishable. The reason is the whole declaration — there is no flag beside it, because a flag can be set and a reason cannot be set without writing one. An executable proof always wins over it, so a rule that acquires a case stops being review-enforced without anyone remembering to delete anything.

objects.title: Every blocking rule names what proves it, and every path it names is in the tree
objects.description: A rule could name a behavioural case in English prose, and nothing noticed when that case was renamed or deleted; the rule went on reading as enforced. The gate holds both halves of the relation. A named path that is not in the tree is `dangling` and is never ratcheted, because a proof that does not exist is worse than no proof. A blocking rule naming neither a validator nor a test nor a reason is `unproven`, which is the half no other check in this repository knows to look for.

objects.title: The effective rule set is resolved as a dependency graph in a deterministic order, and a set that does not resolve is applied by nothing
objects.description: A missing or deprecated dependency, a cycle, one identity claimed twice, a project rule in the vendor namespace, malformed front matter, an unknown key and an x-majordomus block missing its binding are each refused by name. Every dependency is listed before the rule that depends on it, and two runs agree.

objects.title: A rule's proof state is derived from the tree and the ledger together, and a mechanism that refuses violations is never reported as a run that passed
objects.description: `majordomus doctrine` asks whether the repository satisfies a rule now; the proof graph asks whether the rule is in a state where it could be satisfied at all. Ten states, and the ones that must not collapse are `proven` (a passing run and nothing changed since), `gated` (an executable check a CI gate runs, with no verdict recorded here) and `reviewed` (a declared exemption). A rule''s state is the weakest of its parts, so one dangling case makes the rule dangling however many others pass.

objects.title: Opt-in runtime adapters will clamp read size, output size and fan-out from profile-derived limits
objects.description: The one implementation studied was rolled back within days because its limits were global constants rather than task-derived.

objects.title: The Rust executable the rust gate built is published as an artifact with its provenance, and every Rust case drives the executable MAJORDOMUS_BIN names instead of building one
objects.description: scripts/rust-check --artifact DIR copies the debug executable beside a majordomus-cli.json naming the commit, the target triple, the toolchain and the Cargo.lock digest; the workflow uploads it as majordomus-cli-<target>. rust_bin in test/lib.sh hands a case MAJORDOMUS_BIN when set, refuses one that is not executable, builds once with cargo when unset, and asks the case to skip when there is neither; the launcher bin/majordomus-mcp honours the same variable.

objects.title: Coverage of the Rust crate is measured with test code out of the denominator, on every change that can affect the crate and on every push to master, and the build fails under the floor in scripts/rust-coverage-threshold or under the session/continuity domain's own floor in scripts/session-coverage-threshold
objects.description: cargo-llvm-cov over all targets, exported as JSON and post-processed so that tests/, benches/, examples/ and every inline `#[cfg(test)]` item leave the fraction on both sides. --ignore-filename-regex cannot do the second, which is why this is a script and not a flag. Two floors, each one integer in a file of its own, each read by CI, by scripts/rust-check and by just coverage; the domain the second measures is declared in scripts/session-coverage-domain and the script refuses a domain naming a file the export does not carry, so narrowing it to raise the number is a visible edit. Branch coverage proper needs a nightly toolchain; region coverage stands in for it and is reported under that name. The coverage job runs when the plan selects the rust-coverage gate, which the rust and share classes of .ai/repo/ci/gates.yaml select and every full plan does.

objects.title: Every gate the Rust executable must pass is one script, scripts/rust-check, and CI runs that script on every change that can reach the crate
objects.description: Format, lints with warnings as errors (a public item without documentation is one), the suites with the doc examples, rustdoc with warnings denied, the benchmarks building, the registry's own validation, the committed projections in sync, the benchmark coverage complete, and line coverage above the committed floor; --ci adds the benchmark check against the platform's baseline and leaves coverage to its own job, --integration runs the registry checks alone for a change outside the crate. The rust job of the workflow runs the script itself with the mode the plan chose, so there is no second list to fall out of order; the case reads the script, the workflow and the justfile and fails when they disagree; with a toolchain present it also runs the doc examples and builds the benchmarks.

objects.title: The paths of the Rust executable that scale with the repository carry criterion benchmarks that build on every push, and every executable capability declares its benchmark policy, required or waived for a typed reason
objects.description: The YAML subset and front matter, glob matching, the index, the registry, the OpenAPI document, one MCP listing and one capability call (benches/projections.rs); the router, the bridge and the shared server (benches/shared.rs). Numbers are reported, not asserted; no latency budget is promised until one is measured on CI. The capability! macro does not compile an executable without benchmark cases, the registry counts the required and the waived, and the case reads the policy of every executable back through capabilities list.

objects.title: How each declarative kind is read and which keys it may carry is data read at run time, and a repository adds a kind with its JSON Schema without a code change
objects.description: share/kinds.yaml and share/schemas/*.schema.json are the distribution's; .ai/repo/knowledge/kinds.yaml and schemas/ are the repository's; a name declared by both is an error naming both files. The shell tool's allow-lists are generated from the same schemas.

objects.title: What a worker reads of the repository is declared once in .ai/repo/scope.yaml, out wins over in, and the Rust executable discovers, indexes and serves nothing outside it
objects.description: The declaration is typed and schema-validated (share/schemas/majordomus/scope/scope.v1.schema.json; share/allow/scope.txt is generated from it for the shell tool); a repository declaring none is read under the distribution's default and says so; a discovered file outside the scope is an out_of_scope diagnostic naming the rule; a tracked secret is a tracked_secret warning; repository.scope and repository.scope_classify are projected to MCP, HTTP and `majordomus scope`. The crate's tests/scope.rs covers every branch at the library, socket and process level. The doctrine is project.scope-is-declared.

objects.title: A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning
A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout
objects.description: A scope path that escapes the repository root is refused. Starting a second task while one is active is refused.

objects.title: Ranked or semantic retrieval over durable records is deliberately not implemented
objects.description: The corpus is a handful of Markdown files and one JSONL. An index or an embedding store would be a second source of truth that has to be kept in step with the first, and a scan is faster than that problem. Revisited only if a repository appears where the scan is measurably too slow.

objects.title: A provider hook opens the episode below the model and hands the worker what the last one left, records what a compaction is about to discard, and closes the episode with a continuation record beside its envelope
objects.description: The provider's own SessionStart, PreCompact and SessionEnd events draw the boundary and drive the lifecycle; each is idempotent because the events are, and doctor proves the wiring by driving a payload through the end shim with the mutation disabled. The start event writes the policy's briefing to stdout, which is how a continuation record reaches a worker who did not ask for one; the other two write none, because they fire inside a turn already under way. The working context each open freezes is local, appended to rather than rewritten, and refused if it carries a conversation.

objects.title: The session subsystem has a reading of itself — every open episode of the store and not only the one the pointer follows, the episodes that can no longer close themselves, the commit the serving process is answering about, and what each provider's adapter declares
objects.description: continuity.state answers the worker's question about one episode, which is right for a briefing and blind to the other windows open on the same worktree, because state/session-current.yaml is a symlink the most recent start event re-aims. The five lifecycle capabilities read the store, the ledger and the index instead, decide every standing from what the repository can observe, and carry a remedy with every finding. They never write, they judge no thresholds — age is session.freshness and continuity.state's to report — and they declare no command line, because they read .ai/local/ and are served rather than shipped. The Cockpit's Continuity page is their projection and holds no session model of its own.

objects.title: A closed execution episode is a shared object of the layer, written by the tool from git and the ledger, valid against a contract that admits no conversation and no absolute path, and discovered rather than registered
objects.description: The record lives under the manifest's sessions section. Every field is derived - times from the clock, heads and commits from git, the reference lists from the ledger's events for the episode - and the body is the only authored part. The repository is named by its remote and the working copy by a hash, so the resolver can tell one checkout's records from another's without disclosing a path. One source class discovers them; the index, MCP, the object routes, the graph and the site follow.

objects.title: One policy will be shared across repositories and workers

The site is deployed by one script, scripts/site-deploy, from a terminal or from the publication workflow; it refuses a dirty tree, a commit master does not contain and a build that is not HEAD's, pushes site/public to gh-pages with the source commit named, and pushes nothing when the output is unchanged
objects.description: The case runs the whole path against a local bare remote, no network; the footer of every page names the commit, so a deploy is verifiable with curl. The workflow calls the same script with --skip-build after its gate. Pointing GitHub Pages at the branch is a one-time --configure-pages. The hand procedure is .ai/repo/skills/deploy-site/SKILL.md.

objects.title: Publication is gated on everything that can make the published site wrong and waits for nothing else; the checks that decide whether a change may merge run beside it on the same commit, not in front of it
objects.description: The publication path proves the committed derived data current by its input hash, builds the site from it, runs every static check over the output and pushes gh-pages, in one job triggered directly by a master push on paths derived from the gate model; superseded runs are cancelled; the suite, the crate gates, coverage, the macOS suite, the benchmark check and the browser probe run in validate.yml on the same commit and gate merging. The case proves the trigger, the derived paths, the cancellation, the permissions, that no heavy gate is on the path and none left validate.yml, and that a build which skips the generation is byte for byte one that does not.

objects.title: The site's Registry page is rendered from site/data/registry/registry.json, a dataset majordomus generate site derives from the registry and the index with their fingerprints, and generate --check refuses a stale one in CI
objects.description: Every builtin descriptor in full with the file it was composed in, every module with its ids, every object of the layer without its content, every kind with its schema, the declared provider projections, the command line as clap declares it, the MCP tools and resources, the HTTP routes, the benchmark targets, coverage, policy and accepted baselines, and the registry and index fingerprints (majordomus-site-registry/v2); no timestamps of its own, no absolute paths, no git state. The directory is the Rust executable's alone, the shell site generator owns site/data/generated/ wholesale, so no directory has two writers. A canonical object added to the layer changes the fingerprint and the dataset and leaves the bootstraps alone; an exposure removed from a descriptor moves the routes and the coverage and nothing else; the test follows each mutation to exactly the projection it concerns.

objects.title: A skill is one directory under the layer's skills section holding SKILL.md, discovered by the source class `skill` the shell tool and the Rust executable both read, so that adding the file is the whole registration and the catalogue, the command, doctor, MCP and the site all derive from it
objects.description: share/kinds.yaml declares the kind, share/schemas/majordomus/skill/skill.v1.schema.json its contract, and the source classes skill and skill_example in .ai/repo/knowledge/sources.yaml which files carry it. Nothing else names a skill. lib/skills.sh derives one catalogue from that discovery for `skills list|show|check`, the doctrine validator and scripts/generate-site-data; the Rust index serves the same files as majordomus://skill/<id> resources, through majordomus_list and majordomus_get, with no code that knows the kind. The case adds, breaks, renames and removes a skill and watches every surface follow.

objects.title: Every skill is validated against the allow-list generated from its schema, its directory, its sections and its references, a violation names the file and every reason, and a repository with no skills is reported rather than passed
objects.description: `skills check` and the doctrine majordomus.skill-integrity (dispatched by doctor and watch) run one examination — unknown keys, schema version, integer version, closed status set, id equal to the directory, non-empty Purpose, Procedure and Output sections, duplicate ids, descriptions that do not tell two skills apart, related ids that resolve, examples with a heading — and print the counts of what they examined. The site generator refuses to build from a skill that does not validate.

objects.title: The website's skills section is rendered from the skills catalogue, one page per skill carrying the skill's own body and examples, and a removed or renamed skill leaves no page, entry or link behind
objects.description: site/data/generated/skills.json and site/content/skills/ are written by the generator from lib/skills.sh's catalogue, the content directory replaced whole on every run; generate-site-data --check exits 10 when a skill changed or the projection was edited by hand, and CI runs that check before the site builds.

objects.title: The behavioural suite runs a bounded number of cases at a time with the serial runner's semantics, a case that writes into the checkout declares itself exclusive and runs alone, and the parallel phase fails naming the paths when the checkout changed under it
objects.description: MJ_TEST_JOBS bounds the pool (xargs -P, never a bare ampersand); each case has its own log; the verdicts are rendered in name order with a failing case's whole log before its line; a filter that matches nothing and an empty case directory are usage errors in both modes; MJ_TEST_REPORT writes one row per case for the summary. test/cases/26_ci_wiring.sh proves the failure semantics through both modes on a private harness.

objects.title: A task will know which commits it produced, rather than inferring them from a range
objects.description: Today scope is checked with git diff base..HEAD, and a commit range has no author, so another session committing to the same branch in the same checkout has its files counted as this task's work. Recording each commit as it happens turns the question from a heuristic about ranges into an enumeration. The list would be a lookup that git overrules, never authority, and a rewritten commit would be reported as unrecognised rather than resolved to a guess.

objects.title: A task record has no dependencies; sequencing between sessions is not represented
objects.description: Refused for task records, and only for them. Issues and milestones do carry dependencies, validated as two graphs — see docs/ROADMAP.md and docs/PLANNING.md. What stays refused is a task, the record of one session's work, waiting on another; one task is active per checkout and coordination between checkouts is the scope overlap report. The original wording said no dependency graph existed anywhere, which stopped being true when the plan model landed.

objects.title: Execution telemetry will be recorded once a provider exposes it honestly
objects.description: Nothing measures token spend today. Any estimated_ field is labelled and excluded from enforcement.

objects.title: The tool runs read-only from any location, and two locations of one version agree about one repository
objects.description: A checkout copy, an unrelated absolute path and a PATH install read the same repository files and write nothing into the distribution, whose hash is the same after every command. The distribution root is derived from the entry point, never from the environment.

objects.title: The definition of done reaches every generated provider bootstrap as a fragment rendered from share/completion.yaml by the shell tool and the executable to the same bytes; a bootstrap whose source moved fails generate --check, a hand-edited one fails doctor, and regeneration is the only remedy
objects.description: The fragment is COMPLETION_CONTRACT in every template under share/providers/ and .ai/repo/providers/, one plain list item per stage with the questions that belong to it; mj_completion_fragment (lib/update.sh) and CompletionPolicy::bootstrap_fragment (apps/majordomus-cli/src/gates/policy.rs) render it, and the stamp of the rendered body is what holds the two to the same bytes.

objects.title: An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text
objects.description: no_match means the work was done and the thing sought does not exist. failed means the work could not be done. They are different facts.

objects.title: Every public command is named and run by an active use case, a guaranteed claim or an MCP tool without one is a named gap, and the policy says which gaps fail doctor, check and finish
objects.description: The tally is computed from the command registry, docs/CLAIMS.yaml, the executable's registry and the use cases under .ai/repo/use-cases/; a draft never counts. The doctrine is majordomus.use-case-coverage, gated by policy use_cases.coverage and the finish key use_cases_covered.

objects.title: A use case's scenario executes against the real tool in a disposable repository, every step's exit code and output are asserted, and the normalised evidence is what the site shows
objects.description: majordomus usecase run writes .ai/local/evidence/use-cases/<id>.json; scripts/generate-site-data runs the same scenarios and embeds the evidence into site/data/generated/catalogue.json, so --check proves the pages show what the tool did. Paths, timestamps, ids, hashes and durations are normalised; nothing behavioural is.

objects.title: From the files a change touched, the tool names the commands, rules, use cases, scenarios and behavioural cases affected, and scaffolds a draft for a capability no use case covers
objects.description: usecase impact maps paths through docs/RESPONSIBILITIES.yaml, the dispatch table, the rules' identities and the scenarios' fixtures; usecase scaffold writes drafts from the registry, the command fixture and the claims, and never a guarantee.

objects.title: The rule baseline is vendored into the repository with a manifest naming every file and its hash, and a hand edit is detected and refused
objects.description: rules vendor status reports an edited, missing or stray file; rules vendor update refuses over it until --force, and never touches rules/project/. A newer executable reports a newer package and does not apply it.

objects.title: /docs serves this repository's documentation and /swagger serves the Swagger UI, and neither may take the other's mount
objects.description: The Swagger UI held /docs until documentation arrived and wanted the name it had already been given. The case asserts the mounts as data before asserting them as routes, refuses a Swagger producer at /docs, and proves the documentation mount does not swallow /swagger or /openapi.json once it is built. Unbuilt documentation answers 503 naming the command that builds it rather than the viewer that used to answer there.

objects.title: Every web surface is declared once at its producer and resolved into one topology, from which the router, the landing page and the machine-readable index are each projected
objects.description: A surface is a mount, a producer, a kind, a category, a visibility and the provenance of each; the routes the executable answers come from the capability declarations that already exist, a generated directory declares itself beside its output, and the application's site is read from the site generator's configuration. There is no central list. The case asks the page and the index independently and requires the same set of public mounts, so a link written into the page by hand fails it.

objects.title: An operational moment is one file under the layer, discovered rather than registered, and answered by the command line, the HTTP API, the OpenAPI document, MCP, the derived graph and the website with nothing else changed
objects.description: Removing the file removes it from all of them, which is what a hidden registry would fail.

objects.title: A diagnosis of a reader's own symptoms is deterministic counting over the catalogue's metadata, and every recommendation names the moments that produced it
objects.description: No weighting and no percentage; the questionnaire on the website and `majordomus why diagnose` run the same arithmetic over the same data.

objects.title: Every reference a moment makes resolves against the thing it names, and one that does not is an error carrying the nearest candidate
objects.description: Audiences, areas and related moments against the catalogue; commands, capabilities, claims, rules and use cases against their own registries.

objects.title: Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs
objects.description: The path must exist, be executable, and be invoked by the named dispatcher. A hook that invokes it and discards the exit code counts as not wired.

objects.title: A misplaced worktree is brought to its canonical path with its modified, staged, unstaged and untracked work intact, verified by a fingerprint taken before and after the move, and a step is reported as moved only when the two are equal
objects.description: The plan changes nothing and is recomputed under the repository lock before it is applied. Git moves the directory in one rename; the container's occupant goes out to a staging path and then in; a move across filesystems is refused unless a copy is permitted, and then verified against a manifest of every entry before the original is removed. Nothing is reset, stashed, cleaned, checked out or overwritten: a destination that exists is a named conflict, a locked worktree waits, a detached one is never moved, and a session's scratch checkout is reported and moved only on request.

objects.title: A task record names the checkout it belongs to, and another checkout is never held to its scope
objects.description: The record is checkout-local and never tracked, so it does not travel through git; one that arrives by other means is recognised by the worktree it names. check, finish --check and watch report a foreign record and enforce nothing from it; finish refuses to write to it. A record from before the field existed is treated as local, so upgrading does not turn an installation red.

objects.title: A branch's worktree path is derived from git identity and the branch name alone — the primary checkout's sibling named with -wt, then the branch with its hierarchy kept — and is the same answer from every directory of every worktree, with nothing registered or configured
objects.description: The identity is the common git directory and the main worktree git lists first, never the current directory, so a linked worktree does not derive a container inside itself. The branch name is validated by git's reference rules and the derived path is proved on every call to stay below the container. Every registered worktree gets a standing and every condition a stable code with a remedy; the four worktree.* capabilities project the same typed topology to MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, the Swagger UI and the Cockpit, and the pre-commit hook asks the guard.

objects.title: adr
objects.description: The repository's architecture decisions as objects: list, show, ask for the next free identity, propose one with provenance, and validate the whole set against this tree and every other ref.

objects.title: archive
objects.description: Take a snapshot of the tracked tree that can be read, or checked, somewhere else.

objects.title: bench
objects.description: Time every public command of the registry, cold and warm, and compare with the baseline.

objects.title: capture
objects.description: Record the person's raw prompts from a provider hook as a record with its renderings, draw the episode boundary from the provider's own lifecycle hooks, install those hooks, reconcile and prune the archive, and report what each provider actually does here.

objects.title: check
objects.description: Is the current task still consistent with its policy, its scope and this checkout?

objects.title: checkpoint
objects.description: Record compact progress inside the active task, so the next worker does not start over.

objects.title: context
objects.description: What the next worker needs to know now, in authority order and within a budget.

objects.title: decision
objects.description: Record a decision that was made between real alternatives, with its reason, and read them back.

objects.title: doctor
objects.description: Is Majordomus itself healthy, and is every enforcement it declares actually wired here?

objects.title: doctrine
objects.description: What rules are enforced, by what, and whether each one is actually wired.

objects.title: evidence
objects.description: Record evidence against the active task: one obligation it declared, discharged, or one validation gate of the CI model that has reported — each as a ledger line carrying the hash of the files it was taken over.

objects.title: finish
objects.description: Evaluate the finish contract and refuse the outcome if any line of it is unmet.

objects.title: handover
objects.description: Write an append-only continuation record, and resolve the most relevant prior one.

objects.title: help
objects.description: Print the usage text, which is the list of every public command.

objects.title: history
objects.description: Read the append-only ledger back, filtered by task, event or time.

objects.title: init
objects.description: Create the .ai/ layer in this repository, and refuse to overwrite an existing one.

objects.title: knowledge
objects.description: The compiled index over what this repository states.

objects.title: migrate
objects.description: Move pre-.ai project data from .majordomus/ into .ai/, explicitly and backed up.

objects.title: plan
objects.description: The milestone and issue model — validate it, read it, and move one issue through it.

objects.title: prompt
objects.description: List, show and render the repository's own prompt assets, substituting known tokens only.

objects.title: question
objects.description: Open a question that blocks acceptance, resolve it, and list what is still open.

objects.title: recover
objects.description: Close episodes nobody ended, fold duplicate records, classify the stores' stray files.

objects.title: rules
objects.description: The effective rule set, vendored baseline plus project rules.

objects.title: search
objects.description: Find a durable record without reading all of them, in authority order.

objects.title: session
objects.description: Open, inspect and close one execution episode.

objects.title: skills
objects.description: The repository's skills — provider-neutral procedures under the skills section — listed, shown and checked from the one catalogue every surface reads.

objects.title: start
objects.description: Begin one scoped task under a profile, and refuse while another is active.

objects.title: update
objects.description: Regenerate every provider instruction file from the one policy, deterministically.

objects.title: usecase

objects.title: version
objects.description: Print the version, without needing a repository or an installation.

objects.title: watch
objects.description: What has drifted since the last update — policy, projections, state, retention.

objects.title: Milestones
objects.description: One outcome each, written as the problem it ends and the state that proves it ended.

objects.title: Prompt assets

objects.title: Provider templates
objects.description: The one source each provider bootstrap is rendered from; the files at the root are output.

objects.title: Published releases

objects.title: Repository rules
objects.description: The rule object format, where rules live, how they are loaded and composed.

objects.title: Project rules
objects.description: The rules this repository wrote for itself, one file each, resolved with the vendored baseline.

objects.title: Session records
objects.description: One immutable record per closed execution episode, derived from git and the ledger and shared with every surface.

objects.title: Skills

objects.title: Use cases
objects.description: The tasks people perform with the tool, each one a file with the commands, rules and claims it names and the scenario section that proves it.

objects.title: Why this tool exists
objects.description: The operational moments this tool answers, the audiences that recognise them and the areas they fall under, each one a file that every projection is derived from.

objects.title: Workflows
objects.description: The multi-step processes a worker follows here, and when each applies.

objects.title: External workspaces
objects.description: One declaration per external workspace this repository is authorised to read; the content it names is this checkout's state and is never here.

objects.title: The Majordomus layer, served from one machine
objects.description: One shared-CPU machine that stops when idle, serving this repository's AI layer over HTTP, MCP and the generated site.

An architecture decision is one file under the layer's adrs section, validated against the decision contract, with an identity nothing else claims, reciprocal supersession, and every reference it makes resolving

`majordomus adr propose` writes a decision with status proposed and refuses to write any other status, allocates its identity under a lock so concurrent workers never collide, and records what the decision was derived from
A decision states what it put in force as typed references, each one validated, and the reverse direction is read from the knowledge graph rather than written down a second time
The install command this project advertises is run, from the published site, and proved to work
The repository's AI layer is one directory whose manifest names every section, readable without the tool
An archive that lost the file modes fails rather than travelling
Every authored file in this repository is spelled in English
Every externally callable operation of the Rust executable is a benchmark target with a denominator generated from the registry, and a missing case fails the structural check
An unparseable question blocks acceptance exactly as an unresolved one does
A blocking question keeps blocking after the work is handed to a new task
Provider instruction files are thin bootstraps that point at the AI layer and carry no rule of their own
A profile names a capability class rather than a vendor model
A capability of the Rust executable is declared once and composed into its module, the root composes modules, and the registry refuses a capability outside its module's namespace
Every capability of the Rust executable is defined once, and the registry refuses a duplicate id or a colliding projection name, naming both parties
A use case cannot name something the tool does not have
A profile sets how often a worker should checkpoint, and a stale task is reported
A checkpoint is a capped progress record, and a body over the cap is refused
A change runs the gates its paths can affect, decided by one model of what affects what, and a change to the pipeline itself or a path the model does not know runs every gate
No pull request can be merged into the default branch while the verdict status is red, because a branch rule requires it

The verdict status is green only when planning succeeded and every gate the plan selected ran in a job that succeeded; a failed or cancelled job, a selected gate whose job was skipped, or a plan that selected nothing is red

Every command of the Rust executable's command line carries a summary, a long description, help on every argument and at least one example, and every example shown to a reader is executed against the built executable
Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed rather than remembered
The public command surface is declared, and reconciled against the dispatcher
The outcome completed is refused while the completion report says complete is false, and every surface reads that one report
check reports whether state, scope, blockers and checkpoint age are consistent right now
The context a worker is given is assembled from durable state in authority order
The always-loaded instruction file has a line budget with a failing check
Every directory of the layer carries a context document, the exemption is declared by the contract that governs the subtree, and a descendant may narrow that requirement but never weaken it
The context that applies to a path is composed from the layer's scoped documents, root to target, in one deterministic order with provenance, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing

The impact of a change set on the scoped context is reported from git — the documents, the scopes below them, moves with their ancestry, tracked sources to review, and stale projections — and an unrelated change reports nothing
The assembled context obeys a line budget, and every section it drops is named
Every continuity store is proven reachable through its own command
Cost per accepted outcome will be reported from measured data only
A cycle, a self-dependency and a dependency on an issue that does not exist are each refused by name
A decision record without a task, a head and a reason is reported
A decision is recorded with its reason, and superseded rather than edited
Every surface a change reaches is asked what it serves, and a stale or silent one refuses
Every committed derived artifact is regenerated by one command in dependency order and checked by one read-only command
A commit whose derived data is behind its canonical inputs is refused before it exists
What the tool knows about itself is written once and derived everywhere else
Wiring is found in a hook or in any subhook of the directory it dispatches to
Every platform, artifact name and installation URL is derived from one model, and a projection that disagrees with it is refused
State read back is labelled exact, advanced, diverged or different_context against git
A doctrine's class decides whether a violation stops the command
Every enforced rule is declared once, and doctor proves it is reached
watch reports policy, projection, state, scope, handover, verification, staleness and retention drift
Escalating reasoning effort after repeated blocked attempts is recorded rather than assumed
The ledger's event vocabulary is closed, on the way in and on the way out
A run recorded against this commit and a run whose inputs merely have not changed since are reported as different states, never as one
An issue cannot be completed while a required piece of evidence is missing
Every claim names the test that proves it and every test names the claims it proves, from one derivation
Recording one test's result never erases the evidence recorded for any other test
A claim's proof is an execution that was recorded with the commit it ran against, not a test path that resolves
A claim that declares a guarantee no recorded run supports is named by a gate rather than displayed as guaranteed
The site's pages about the Rust executable are derived from the registry, and a capability that joins or leaves it gains or loses its page from the generators alone
A cached capability of the Rust executable answers the same value uncached, cold and warm, a hit runs no handler, errors and commands are never cached, and the key carries the registry fingerprint
Execution waves are computed from the graph, and issues in one wave that touch the same paths are reported as serialised
Exit codes are a contract, and no code means "warn and continue"
finish evaluates the finish contract line by line and refuses when any line is unmet

Every generated artifact declares the document it projects, the encoding it is written in, the schema its content satisfies and its source, and a structured document is written in every encoding it is committed in from one value
The committed projections, the OpenAPI document, the capability reference and the allow-lists, are regenerated from the registry and the schemas, and generate --check refuses a stale one
Identity fields on every state record are computed from git and never authored
A projection that stops being applied turns a build red, and a gate that cannot reach GitHub reports that it cannot rather than passing
GitHub milestones and issues are generated from the canonical model, and a hand-edited generated region is reported rather than overwritten
handover writes an append-only record with computed front matter and required sections
The ledger is readable back as operational history
After startup, no MCP or HTTP request of the Rust executable scans the repository, builds the index or the registry, derives a schema or builds a projection, and perf.counters proves it
Installing into a repository that already has an installation is refused
The documented one-line install command is composed from the model's parts, and a document that states a different one fails the suite
The installer verifies an artifact's digest and inspects its archive before anything is unpacked, and any failure leaves the previous installation working
MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI, the capabilities commands and the generated reference are derived from the registry, and a change to one definition reaches every one of them
The homepage names nothing of its own
Every line of the ledger is a well-formed event
A repository on the pre-.ai layout is migrated once, explicitly, with a previewed plan and a verified backup of its local state, and the command is idempotent afterwards
Checkout-local state lives under .ai/local/, is ignored by git, and is absent on a fresh clone or worktree
An MCP client opened in the repository starts the server itself, building the executable when it must, through the client configurations at the root and bin/majordomus-mcp
What the MCP server serves is decided by the manifest, the declared source classes and each file's front matter, so an object added to the layer is served with no change to the executable
A file of the layer the MCP server cannot read is excluded with a diagnostic naming its path and the index says it is degraded, never silently smaller

A server whose lease was taken over says so on the endpoint every reader probes, refuses to take on a new client, and reports that what its health describes is another process; the sessions it already had continue and it ends with them

Nothing a client leaves behind locks another client out of the shared server; a corrupt, empty, stale or abandoned lease is taken over and named, a client that cannot share is served alone with the reason logged, and a signal removes the lease before the server dies

Every client attached to the shared server is a peer named by its own initialize, listed by majordomus_peers, and majordomus_announce tells the others what it is working on and which paths it expects to touch

One shared server serves a repository: the first majordomus mcp binds loopback HTTP with Swagger UI and MCP over HTTP beside its stdio session and logs the URL, every later one attaches to it, and it ends when the last client leaves
The Rust executable serves the repository's AI layer to an MCP client over stdio, read-only, with protocol frames alone on stdout

A majordomus:// URI resolves the same way through the MCP resource read, the majordomus_get tool and the HTTP object route, and majordomus://repository answers repository.info as a JSON document tagged builtin
A discovered node — trusted or not — gains no execution, no authorization and no write surface; trust labels records under an explicit policy that defaults to deny_unknown
No mesh discovery socket opens until the repository commits an enabled mesh declaration, and a disabled or absent declaration is reported as the reason, not an error

Every discovery observation converges into one bounded registry, deduplicated by node identity across sources, replay-protected per instance, and every surface projects that registry and holds no peers of its own
A profile declares which context a worker should load and no more
The model catalogue reports whether a vendor's named credential variable is set and can carry no secret value — the schema has no field one could hide in
Vendors and models are declared once in share/models.yaml, and the CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and Cockpit render that one declaration with no model name of their own
A routing decision names why the selected model was selected and, for every excluded model, the first check it failed — the same answer for the same question, with no hidden state
Every executable line, function and region a change adds or touches in the Rust crate is covered by a test; new debt is refused and untouched legacy debt is left alone
A hardcoded count in the always-loaded file is a failure
Nothing performs a network call, evaluates generated text, or deletes recursively
A hand-edited instruction file is never silently overwritten
Handovers carry durable facts, never conversation transcripts
A task that declares obligations reaches the outcome completed only when each one has evidence, and evidence taken over files that have since changed no longer discharges anything
An obligation whose fact the tool can hold is established live rather than recorded, and a hand-recorded line neither discharges it nor rescues it
An unresolved question blocks acceptance, and an unparseable entry is a failure

The OpenAPI document is inferred: the tags are the modules, the examples are the benchmark cases, the responses are the router's statuses by kind, the prose is the one text every projection shares, and the site's API reference is rendered from the committed document
Overlap between parallel workers is computed on claimed paths in both containment directions
Every repository-relative reference in the always-loaded file is proven to resolve
The canonical policy is parsed and rejected if it contains an unknown key
A product feature is discovered, never registered
The public dataset carries only fields somebody allowed
A reference that resolves to nothing is an error, not a broken link
What a feature is on is derived; what it is for is written
Capability class, reasoning effort, output verbosity, context and verification are five independent axes
Every profile is parsed, its unknown keys rejected, and the default profile proven to exist
Milestones and issues are canonical repository files, and a key nobody reads is an error
Issue and milestone status is derived from recorded facts and is stored nowhere
Every generated instruction file carries its own stamp, and a hand edit is detected
Provider instruction files are generated from the one policy, deterministically
A prompt renders against a closed set of tokens, and an unknown token is an error
Every prompt asset renders, and an unknown token is a failure
A provider hook captures the person's raw prompts below the model, as a record and a rendering, and doctor proves it by running it
A captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or records that none could be resolved; the archive is private, bounded and free of credential material
The provider bootstraps are a target of `majordomus generate`, rendered by one renderer, and `generate --check` refuses a stale one in CI
The right prior record is resolved by worktree and branch, and an unrelated one is never offered
Rotating the ledger archives the oldest lines and never deletes them
Durable records are searchable literally, across kinds, without an index
A projection can own only the region between its markers
A release archive carries every path once and carries nothing but files and directories
A release publishes an artifact for every supported target or it is not published
Every finding carries the command that reproduces it
The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked
The roadmap is derived from milestone state, and no document may be a second authority for it
Routing recommendations will be derived from measured cost and outcome data
A rule that no program can express says so, with the reason, and is counted apart
Every blocking rule names what proves it, and every path it names is in the tree
The effective rule set is resolved as a dependency graph in a deterministic order, and a set that does not resolve is applied by nothing
A rule's proof state is derived from the tree and the ledger together
Opt-in runtime adapters will clamp read size, output size and fan-out from profile-derived limits
The Rust executable the rust gate built is published as an artifact with its provenance, and every Rust case drives the executable MAJORDOMUS_BIN names instead of building one

Coverage of the Rust crate is measured with test code out of the denominator, on every change that can affect the crate and on every push to master, and the build fails under the floor in scripts/rust-coverage-threshold or under the session/continuity domain's own floor in scripts/session-coverage-threshold
Every gate the Rust executable must pass is one script, scripts/rust-check, and CI runs that script on every change that can reach the crate

The paths of the Rust executable that scale with the repository carry criterion benchmarks that build on every push, and every executable capability declares its benchmark policy, required or waived for a typed reason
How each declarative kind is read and which keys it may carry is data read at run time, and a repository adds a kind with its JSON Schema without a code change
What a worker reads of the repository is declared once in .ai/repo/scope.yaml, out wins over in, and the Rust executable discovers, indexes and serves nothing outside it
A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning
A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout
Ranked or semantic retrieval over durable records is deliberately not implemented
A provider hook opens and closes the execution episode, and the context it was given at the open is frozen beside it
The session subsystem can be watched, not only used: every open episode, what cannot close itself, and which commit the process is answering about

A closed execution episode is a shared object of the layer, written by the tool from git and the ledger, valid against a contract that admits no conversation and no absolute path, and discovered rather than registered
One policy will be shared across repositories and workers
The site is deployed by one script, from a terminal or from the Pages workflow, and the deploy names its source

Publication is gated on everything that can make the published site wrong and waits for nothing else; the checks that decide whether a change may merge run beside it on the same commit, not in front of it
The site's Registry page is rendered from a dataset `majordomus generate site` derives from the registry, and `generate --check` refuses a stale one
A skill is one directory under the skills section, discovered by the source class both readers share, so that adding the file is the whole registration
Every skill is validated against the allow-list generated from its schema, its directory, its sections and its references, and a repository with no skills is reported rather than passed
The website's skills section is rendered from the skills catalogue, one page per skill carrying its own body and examples, and a removed or renamed skill leaves nothing behind

The behavioural suite runs a bounded number of cases at a time with the serial runner's semantics, a case that writes into the checkout declares itself exclusive and runs alone, and the parallel phase fails naming the paths when the checkout changed under it
A task will know which commits it produced, rather than inferring them from a range
A task record has no dependencies; sequencing between sessions is not represented
Execution telemetry will be recorded once a provider exposes it honestly
The tool runs read-only from any location, and two locations of one version agree about one repository
The definition of done reaches every generated bootstrap as a fragment both renderers produce byte for byte
An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text
Every public command is named and run by an active use case, a guaranteed claim or an MCP tool without one is a named gap, and the policy says which gaps fail doctor, check and finish
A use case's scenario executes against the real tool in a disposable repository, every step's exit code and output are asserted, and the normalised evidence is what the site shows
From the files a change touched, the tool names the commands, rules, use cases, scenarios and behavioural cases affected, and scaffolds a draft for a capability no use case covers
The rule baseline is vendored into the repository with a manifest naming every file and its hash, and a hand edit is detected and refused
/docs serves this repository's documentation and /swagger serves the Swagger UI, and neither may take the other's mount
Every web surface is declared once at its producer and resolved into one topology, from which the router, the landing page and the machine-readable index are each projected
An operational moment is discovered, never registered
A diagnosis is counting, and it says what it counted
Every reference a moment makes resolves
Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs
A misplaced worktree migrates with its work intact, and proves it
A task record names its checkout, and another checkout is never held to its scope
A branch's worktree path is derived, never registered
Every claim about speed is a recorded measurement
objects.description: The benchmark targets are derived from the registry, so a capability nothing times cannot be merged; runs are compared with a tracked baseline per platform under a regression policy; the shell tool reports where every command's time went; and derived state is computed once per state version rather than per call.

objects.title: CI planned from one model, the site deployed from its verified run
objects.description: The gate model names every validation gate and which classes of paths select it; the workflow is a thin adapter over that plan; the publication path proves the committed derived data current by its input hash and renders it; and the tool supervises its own repository with its own hooks.

objects.title: The Cockpit: the registry rendered for a person
objects.description: At /cockpit the shared server lays out what a capability answered — the registry explorer, every object of the layer, the derived graphs, the directory contracts, the continuity of this checkout, the worktree topology, one health report naming the engine behind every check — and every page is complete HTML before any script runs.

objects.title: Every directory of the layer carries its contract, and a worker reads what applies
objects.description: Every README under .ai/ is a context document with an identity, a scope, the providers and audience it addresses and how it composes with its ancestors; the repository scope declares what a worker reads and what it never reads; and the briefing a worker gets is assembled from durable state within a line budget with every exclusion named.

objects.title: Sessions, prompts and handovers that outlive the conversation
objects.description: Task state, checkpoints, handovers, decisions and open questions live in files outside every conversation; a session opens and closes into an immutable record; the person's prompts are captured by the provider's own hooks; and the next episode is briefed from those records, labelled by how far git has moved since.

objects.title: Several agents on one repository, without stepping on each other
objects.description: A task claims its scope before the first edit; check and finish refuse a file outside it and report another worktree's overlapping claim; every client of the shared server is a peer that can announce its intent and paths; and each branch has exactly one worktree, derived from git.

objects.title: New code is covered, measured once and asked two questions
objects.description: scripts/rust-coverage is the one coverage authority: a single cargo-llvm-cov export, test code excluded from both sides of every fraction, one rule for lines, functions and regions. Three questions read that judgment — a crate-wide line floor, the session/continuity domain held to 100%, and the changed-code differential gate that refuses new debt while leaving untouched legacy debt alone. The differential intersects the export with the lines git says a change touched against the branch's merge-base, working tree included, and distinguishes PASS, FAIL, UNKNOWN and BLOCKED so a crashed tool or an unresolvable base is never a silent green.

objects.title: Declare once, derive every interface
objects.description: One typed declaration per capability, one file per object of the layer; every interface, generated document and page is derived from the registry those declarations build, and a stale projection fails the build.

objects.title: A deployment is one canonical object, and every provider artifact is generated from it
objects.description: One deployment object per hosted instance of the executable, validated against the registry this process built; the container image definition, the provider configuration and the smoke expectations are generated from it and checked for drift.

objects.title: Rules a machine decides, wired, tested and CI-blocking
objects.description: Every rule is a portable Markdown object with front matter, and it is enforced in one of three declared modes: a validator the dispatcher runs, a gate or case that proves it, or a stated reason why no program can express it. Doctor walks the dispatch chain from the source, refusing a validator nobody declares and a declaration nothing runs; the proof graph walks the other relation, joining each rule to the tree and to the runs recorded against it, so that a rule naming a case which was deleted is reported as reading enforced rather than being it.

objects.title: A claim is proven by a run that happened, not by a file that exists
objects.description: The claims matrix binds a claim to a test by path, and a path resolving says a file exists rather than that anything ran. The ledger records the latest execution of every test with its provenance; the join is derived on every read and answers, per claim, whether the repository can honestly call it proven, only-not-invalidated, stale, failing or never run.

objects.title: Done is a contract, evaluated line by line and refused when unmet
objects.description: A task starts with a declared scope and a profile; check reports whether the task is consistent with policy, scope and state; finish evaluates the policy's contract — scope respected, verification ran, state updated, no open blockers, a note present — and refuses with the reproducing command when any line fails.

objects.title: One command to install, one to initialise, nothing else to trust
objects.description: One distribution model owns every platform, artifact name and URL; the installer, the release build matrix, the installation guide, the website's install block and the public release metadata are generated from it, and a release publishes an artifact for every supported target or it is not published.

objects.title: One registry over the command line, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI and MCP
objects.description: The Rust executable serves the layer read-only over stdio MCP, MCP over HTTP, routes under /api/v1/, an OpenAPI document with a Swagger UI, and a command line, all derived from the capability registry; one shared server per repository, and every attached client is a peer the others can see.

objects.title: Decisions and knowledge that compound instead of evaporating
objects.description: Decisions are recorded with their reason and their task, open questions block acceptance until resolved, architecture decision records carry typed references to the rules, claims, files and tests they put in force, and the graph of all of it is derived from those references rather than drawn.

objects.title: Running instances find each other, and prove who they are
objects.description: A node is an Ed25519 keypair kept per user and machine; one signed, versioned, bounded envelope travels over every discovery transport; providers only observe while the manager owns the single verification path and the single registry; trust is an explicit policy that defaults to deny_unknown; and nothing opens a socket until the repository commits an enabled mesh declaration. CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and the Cockpit render the same runtime state.

objects.title: The models the world offers, declared once and routed with reasons
objects.description: share/models.yaml declares vendors and models in one place, in routing's preference order, with provenance stated and pricing deliberately absent; models.list and models.route project the catalogue and its explainable routing to the CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and the Cockpit, credential presence is reported without any value being read, and nothing anywhere calls a model — the crate's no-network boundary stands.

objects.title: Milestones and issues as data; status derived, never stored
objects.description: Milestones are outcome specifications and issues are execution contracts, one YAML file each; the dependency graph decides execution waves and the next ready issue; a milestone whose dependencies are not accepted is blocked whatever its own issues say; and the GitHub projection is rendered offline from the same model.

objects.title: One policy, projected into every tool's instruction file
objects.description: A provider-neutral policy and four execution profiles are the one source; majordomus update renders each provider bootstrap from its template, stamps it with the policy hash and the hash of its own content, and doctor fails a bootstrap that was hand-edited, that carries a rule corpus of its own, or that exceeds the always-loaded budget.

objects.title: Every record names the commit, the branch and the episode that made it
objects.description: The ledger records every durable event with its task and its head; identity fields on any record are computed from git and refused when authored; a closed session is an immutable record of what one episode produced; the person's prompts are captured by the provider's hooks; and retention is capped by policy rather than by forgetting.

objects.title: Skills are procedures as data, discovered and checked, never registered
objects.description: A skill is a provider-neutral procedure for one bounded kind of work, front matter under a schema over a body with a purpose, a procedure and an output contract; the source class discovers it, skills check holds every one to its contract, and nothing loads a skill unless the task is about it.

objects.title: Every use case is executed against the tool, not described
objects.description: A use case names the commands, rules, claims and applications it relies on and carries a scenario as data; usecase run executes it in a disposable repository and records normalised evidence; maturity is observed from the evidence; coverage of commands, guaranteed claims and MCP tools is tallied and the policy says which gaps fail.

objects.title: The failure modes it answers are objects, not marketing pages
objects.description: Moments, audiences and areas are kinds of the layer; a moment names the commands, capabilities, claims, rules and use cases that answer it, each reference validated; the catalogue, the questionnaire, the diagnosis and every page and filter are derived from those files.

objects.title: One branch, one worktree, at a path derived from git
objects.description: The container is the primary checkout's sibling named with -wt, a branch's worktree is the branch name under it with its hierarchy kept, both derived from git identity and registered nowhere; a pre-commit guard refuses a feature branch committed from anywhere else, and migration moves a misplaced worktree with its uncommitted work, fingerprinted before and after.

objects.title: Audit what actually plans work in this repository
objects.description: Establish an evidence-backed map of how work is currently planned, tracked and remembered here, so that the model that replaces it is built against reality rather than against the README.

objects.title: Define the canonical milestone and issue schema
objects.description: Define the smallest repository-native representation of a milestone outcome specification and an issue execution contract, and enforce it the way every other configuration file here is enforced: a key nobody reads is an error.

objects.title: Implement the model loader and the status derivation engine
objects.description: Load every canonical file into one normalised model and derive issue and milestone status from recorded facts, in exactly one implementation that every surface calls.

objects.title: Implement DAG validation and execution waves
objects.description: Validate the dependency graph and derive topological execution waves, refusing every malformed graph with a named finding rather than a guess.

objects.title: Implement the plan command surface
objects.description: Give a worker one command that answers what is ready, why something is blocked, what the graph looks like, and that moves an issue through its lifecycle while refusing illegal transitions.

objects.title: Generate the Mermaid DAG from the graph
objects.description: Render the dependency graph as Mermaid from the same edges the engine derives, so that no diagram anywhere is drawn by hand.

objects.title: Enforce the canonical model as doctrine
objects.description: Add the project model to the doctrine registry so that doctor reports a broken model and watch reports a model that has drifted, through the same dispatcher every other rule uses.

objects.title: Project the model to GitHub milestones and issues
objects.description: Create and update GitHub milestones and issues from the canonical model, report drift instead of overwriting human edits, and keep every network call out of the tool itself.

objects.title: Project the model into the website
objects.description: Generate the roadmap, every milestone page, every issue page and the DAG page from the canonical model through the existing site data pipeline.

objects.title: Behavioural tests for schema, status, graph and command
objects.description: Prove each rule of the model with a case that fails when the rule is removed, in a disposable repository, the way every other rule here is proven.

objects.title: Cross-surface consistency and mutation tests
objects.description: Prove that the CLI, the generated site data and the GitHub projection describe the same graph, and that changing one canonical dependency changes all of them.

objects.title: Make CI refuse an invalid model or a stale projection
objects.description: Add the model validation and the projection freshness check to the blocking CI job, with no advisory pass.

objects.title: Document the semantics and the dogfooding rule
objects.description: Write the human documentation that explains why the model exists and what its terms mean, and leave every current fact to be generated.

objects.title: Make the worker instructions require the model
objects.description: Change the always-loaded provider instructions so that a fresh worker of any provider selects work through the model rather than from conversation or a TODO list.

objects.title: Open the first real milestone and execute one issue through it
objects.description: Prove the system on real repository work: open a milestone that exists because the repository needs it, and take one of its issues from READY to DONE entirely through the model.

objects.title: Reproduce the escaped blocker as an executable case
objects.description: Write a behavioural case that runs the documented sequence — open a question, hand over, start a new task, finish completed — and records what happens today, so that the gap stops being a sentence in a claim note and becomes something a command demonstrates.

objects.title: Decide whether a question transfers or the gate widens
objects.description: Choose between the two alternatives the claim names, record the decision with what was rejected and why, and state which case the chosen behaviour is deliberately wrong in.

objects.title: Implement the decision and prove it holds
objects.description: Make the chosen behaviour real in the question store and the blocker gate, and turn the characterisation case from I0101 into a case that fails when the behaviour is removed.

objects.title: Move the claim from planned to guaranteed
objects.description: Update docs/CLAIMS.yaml and the claim's detail page so the public surface states what is now true, with the file that implements it and the test that proves it.

objects.title: Declare which profile axis may become which runtime limit
objects.description: Add one canonical file beside the profiles that maps a profile axis to the runtime limit it may derive, so that a limit has a single source, an axis nobody can enforce cannot be listed, and a limit no adapter applies is a validation error rather than a comment.

objects.title: Resolve a task's effective limits and print them as data
objects.description: Add a read-only command that resolves the limits the active task's profile derives and prints them, in text and as JSON, so that a worker, a wrapper or a test can read the same numbers the enforcement will use.

objects.title: Make enforcement opt-in, and prove a repository that declines is unaffected
objects.description: Add one policy key that turns runtime enforcement on, default it to off, and prove with a case that a repository which never sets it behaves exactly as it does today.

objects.title: Apply one derived limit for real and prove it changes what happens
objects.description: Implement the first adapter: one limit, derived from the profile through the resolver, applied where a provider can honestly apply it, with a behavioural case that fails if the limit stops being applied.

objects.title: Declare the clamp as a doctrine so the mapping and the adapter cannot drift
objects.description: Declare the rule that every applied limit is derived from the declared mapping as a doctrine with its own validator, dispatched from the registry, reaching the command that claims to run it, covered by a case and run in CI.

objects.title: Publish the runtime-adapters claim with the test that proves it and the limits it does not cover
objects.description: Move the runtime-adapters row from planned to guaranteed, citing the adapter and the case, and state on its detail page which axes remain advisory and why, so that the guarantee is narrower than the milestone title rather than as wide as it.

objects.title: Define the execution record, including what an absence looks like
objects.description: Define the durable shape of a task's execution facts: which fields exist, who reported each one, and how a provider that reported nothing is recorded, so that absence is a value with a reason rather than a missing key or a zero.

objects.title: Record telemetry a provider reports, and refuse anything it did not
objects.description: Add the command that attaches measured execution facts to the active task, accepting only values a provider actually reported and refusing any field the caller cannot attribute to a reporter.

objects.title: Prove a silent provider produces an explicit absence, never a guess
objects.description: Write the case that runs a whole task under a provider that reports nothing and asserts that the completed record carries an explicit absence with a reason, and that no field anywhere in the surfaces shows an estimated number.

objects.title: Read the measurements back through the history surface, under a bound
objects.description: Make recorded execution facts readable through the surface that already answers questions about past tasks, with the same retention bound the other durable stores carry.

objects.title: Publish the telemetry claim and record what remains unmeasured
objects.description: Move the telemetry claim to guaranteed for the providers that report honestly, name the implementation and the case, and state in the economics document which providers report nothing and what that costs the analysis.

objects.title: Define an accepted outcome, and join it to its measurements without storing the join
objects.description: Define precisely which finishes count as accepted outcomes, and derive the join between an accepted outcome and the execution facts of the work that produced it from records that already exist, storing no third record.

objects.title: Report cost only where measurement and acceptance both exist
objects.description: Add the command that reports what accepted outcomes cost, computed only from measured facts, and reports no figure at all where either half is missing, saying which half.

objects.title: Make a thin denominator say so rather than average it away
objects.description: Make every reported figure carry the number of accepted outcomes it rests on, refuse to present a single observation as an average, and prove both with cases.

objects.title: Publish the cost-per-outcome claim with its unit defined beside it
objects.description: Move the cost-per-outcome claim to guaranteed, define the unit and the denominator where a reader meets the figure, and state what the number cannot be used to compare.

objects.title: Group comparable work from what the records already carry
objects.description: Derive the grouping that makes two pieces of work comparable from facts the records already hold, so that a recommendation compares like with like without anybody inventing a taxonomy of task types.

objects.title: Recommend a profile from measured cost, naming the measurements
objects.description: Add the command that recommends a profile for a class of work from measured cost per accepted outcome, and prints the measurements the recommendation was derived from alongside it.

objects.title: Return no recommendation where the data is too thin, and say why
objects.description: Make insufficient data produce no recommendation rather than a weak one, with the threshold declared as data and the reason printed, proved by cases on both sides of it.

objects.title: Prove the recommendation is advisory and publish it as such
objects.description: Prove with a case that a recommendation never changes the profile a task runs under, and publish the routing claim stating that Majordomus recommends and does not route.

objects.title: Let a policy name a shared source it does not copy
objects.description: Let a repository's policy name a shared policy source and resolve it offline from the filesystem, so that one statement of a rule can govern more than one repository without being pasted into each.

objects.title: Make a local override explicit and prove it survives an update of the shared source
objects.description: Define how a repository overrides part of a shared policy, require the override to be declared rather than inferred from a value differing, and prove with a case that updating the shared source leaves the override standing.

objects.title: Report drift from the shared policy in one command
objects.description: Report, in one command, every way a repository's effective policy differs from the shared source it names, separating declared overrides from undeclared divergence.

objects.title: Prove the offline guarantee survives sharing
objects.description: Prove with cases and a doctrine that no path introduced by shared policy reaches a network, and that an unavailable shared source degrades to a named refusal rather than a fetch or a silent local fallback.

objects.title: Publish the shared-policy claim and what sharing still cannot do
