objects.description: Move the shared-policy claim to guaranteed, cite the implementation and the cases, and state plainly what a shared policy does not provide: no service, no registry, no cross-machine visibility, and no enforcement of a repository that never adopts it.

objects.title: Reproduce the misattribution as an executable case
objects.description: Write a behavioural case in which two workers share one checkout — one starts a task, the other records a decision — and assert what happens today, so that the defect stops being an anecdote and becomes something a command demonstrates.

objects.title: Decide how a record is attributed, between named alternatives
objects.description: Choose between the alternatives that actually exist — attribute to the session that ran the command, refuse to write when the active task belongs to somebody else, or require the task to be named explicitly — and record the choice with the case each rejected option gets wrong.

objects.title: Implement the decision and prove it holds
objects.description: Implement whatever I0702 decided across every command that writes a durable record, and turn the characterisation case into one that asserts the new behaviour.

objects.title: Publish what attribution guarantees, and what it still cannot
objects.description: State on the public surface what a record's attribution now means, and state plainly what it does not: that a worker's identity is supplied by the session, not verified, and that nothing here proves who a worker was.

objects.title: Narrow the Clean Extraction Boundary and record what was adopted
objects.description: Rewrite the Clean Extraction Boundary in docs/DESIGN.md so that it permits a generic deterministic provenance graph derived from this repository's own artifacts while continuing to exclude everything it excludes today, and record in docs/EXTRACTION_REPORT.md which architectural ideas from the studied prior art were adopted by re-derivation and which were refused, each with its reason.

objects.title: Specify the session record before writing one
objects.description: Define the session object in docs/SCHEMAS.md and docs/CONTINUITY.md: what a session is, how it differs from a task and from a handover, the filename grammar of a closed record, the exact field list, which fields are computed from git, and the rule that the reference envelope is derived rather than accumulated.

objects.title: Open a session and report its status
objects.description: Implement lib/session.sh with `session start` and `session status`: one active session per worktree in .majordomus/state/session-current.yaml, its identity and git facts computed, a second start refused rather than silently replacing the first, and a status that reports the active session against current git or says plainly that none is open.

objects.title: Close a session into an envelope derived from the ledger
objects.description: Implement `session close`: read the active record, derive the episode's references from the ledger between its start and now, write an immutable closed record with computed end-state git facts and an optional authored summary body, remove the active record, and append the close event to the ledger.

objects.title: Read sessions back with a divergence label
objects.description: Implement `session list`, `session show <id>` and `session latest`, each resolving with the established rule — same repository, same worktree, same branch, then same branch — and each printing the existing divergence label of the record against current git.

objects.title: Make the session rules doctrines, with retention and archiving
objects.description: Declare the session rules in share/standard/majordomus/ with validators that doctor and watch dispatch — a malformed active or closed record, a session left open past its policy, a reference to a record that does not exist, and retention over the declared cap — and implement policy-driven archiving that never deletes and never overwrites.

objects.title: Discover knowledge sources from git, not from the filesystem
objects.description: Implement the discovery stage of lib/knowledge.sh: a declared list of source classes, each with a scope of shared or operational, resolved through git ls-files for tracked repository artifacts and through the known state paths for operational records, producing a deterministic ordered list of sources with their content hashes.

objects.title: Extract nodes with identities that survive a rebuild
objects.description: Implement the extract and normalise stages in lib/knowledge.awk: one node per canonical object, with an identity derived from its canonical id or its repository path, a kind that is only asserted when a structural fact establishes it, and a title taken from the record or from the document's first heading.

objects.title: Record only edges that a file states, each with where it was observed
objects.description: Implement the resolve and graph stages: edges derived from the explicit relationships the canonical files already declare — claim to source, implementation and test; issue to milestone and to its dependencies; evidence to issue; doctrine to validator, claim and test; record to task — each carrying the file and field it was observed in, and none carrying a relationship inferred from prose.

objects.title: A content-hash manifest that makes a second sync cheap
objects.description: Implement the manifest: one row per source with its path, content hash, extractor version and the node ids it produced, written beside the generated graph, compared on every sync, and used so that a sync with no source change does no extraction and says so.

objects.title: Read-only knowledge lookup with an ordering that can be explained
objects.description: Implement `knowledge search`, `knowledge show` and `knowledge related`: deterministic lookup over the generated index with a documented, tested match order, JSON output that names the field each result matched on, and no write of any kind.

objects.title: Validate the graph, and let doctor and watch ask the same validator
objects.description: Implement `knowledge validate` detecting duplicate node ids, dangling explicit references, source paths that no longer exist, hash mismatches, edges with a missing end, edges without provenance and a stale generated index, each with a severity and a reproduce command, and declare the rule in the doctrine registry so doctor and watch dispatch the same validator rather than reimplementing it.

objects.title: A closed session becomes a node that points at its episode
objects.description: Extract closed sessions as knowledge nodes whose edges point at the tasks, issues, checkpoints, handovers, decisions and questions they name, so that the graph answers which sessions touched an issue, which decisions affected it, and which handover continued a task — without any session body being copied anywhere.

objects.title: Give the worker a bounded slice of knowledge, not the knowledge base
objects.description: Add a knowledge section to `majordomus context`, selected deterministically from what the active task and issue already reference, capped by a profile toggle and an item limit, dropped before any immutable fact when the budget is short, and named under EXCLUDED whenever it is dropped or switched off.

objects.title: Say what is now true in the claims, the documentation and the worker instructions
objects.description: Add the behavioural claims this milestone earns to docs/CLAIMS.yaml with real implementation and test paths, document the commands in docs/CLI.md, correct the sentence in docs/CONTINUITY.md that says no index is maintained, write docs/KNOWLEDGE.md, and extend the provider-neutral instruction source so a fresh worker knows the session and knowledge steps of the lifecycle.

objects.title: Prove the loop on a real issue, without a transcript
objects.description: Execute the whole lifecycle against a real issue of this repository — session start, plan next, plan show, context, knowledge retrieval, work, checkpoint and decision, evidence, plan done, session close, knowledge sync, watch — and record as evidence what a following session could determine from the records alone.

objects.title: Phase timing and work counters behind MJ_TIMING
objects.description: Time every validator and count every YAML flatten and git call when MJ_TIMING is set, and report them ranked at exit.

objects.title: The command registry is read in one pass
objects.description: Replace the per-index, per-field awk lookups in mj_cmdreg_public, mj_cmdreg_ids and the event registry with one awk pass each, and read them once per process.

objects.title: The project model is loaded with one flatten per file and no per-file lookups
objects.description: Make mj_project_load and mj_project_unknown_keys read each milestone and issue once, checking ids and unknown keys inside awk rather than with a subprocess per file and per key.

objects.title: Catalogue, DAG, context and command-surface validators read their inputs once
objects.description: Rewrite the remaining validators that loop mj_yget or mj_git per item so that each reads its inputs with one pass.

objects.title: Flattened YAML is cached under .ai/local/cache by content hash
objects.description: Cache the output of mj_yaml_flatten under .ai/local/cache/flat/<sha256>, keyed by the file's content hash and the flattener's own version, so a second command on unchanged files does no parsing.

objects.title: Every canonical file is flattened at most once per command
objects.description: Add a case that runs doctor, watch, context and plan validate under MJ_TIMING and asserts the yaml_flatten count never exceeds the number of distinct canonical files a command reads.

objects.title: majordomus bench: targets derived from the command registry
objects.description: Add the bench command: every public command in share/commands.yaml is a target, run against a disposable installed repository, with warmup and samples from the policy, reporting min, p50, p90, p95, p99, max, mean and stddev per target and mode.

objects.title: Bench persists local runs and keeps a latest projection
objects.description: Write every run to .ai/local/benchmarks/runs/<run-id>.json and .ai/local/benchmarks/latest.json atomically, and append one line per run to history.jsonl.

objects.title: An explicit committed baseline
objects.description: Add bench --write-baseline, which refuses a dirty tree unless forced, prints old, new and delta per target, and writes .ai/repo/benchmarks/baseline.json with schema majordomus/benchmark-baseline/v1.

objects.title: bench --check refuses a regression by policy
objects.description: Compare a fresh run against the baseline under the policy's benchmark.regression thresholds (relative p50, p95, p99) and exit non-zero naming the command, the metric, both values and the threshold.

objects.title: The benchmark policy block
objects.description: Declare benchmark.samples, benchmark.warmup, benchmark.timeout_seconds, benchmark.cache_max_entries, benchmark.regression.p50/p95/p99 and benchmark.budget.doctor_ms in the policy, its allow-list and the skeleton, with no reader-side default.

objects.title: doctor under a declared budget, and the hook inherits it
objects.description: Report doctor's own wall time against benchmark.budget.doctor_ms as a finding, advisory, and record the measured value on this repository as the budget's rationale in docs/PERFORMANCE.md.

objects.title: Performance doctrine as project rules
objects.description: Add project rules: derived state is computed once per state version, a command's hot path does not re-parse canonical files, every public command is benchmarkable from the registry, cacheability never changes observable behaviour, and performance claims need benchmark evidence.

objects.title: docs/PERFORMANCE.md, README, CONTRIBUTING and CLI reference
objects.description: Write the reference: goals, phases and counters, batch reads, the flatten cache, cold versus warm, result and baseline schemas, the policy block, the regression workflow, the contributor workflow and the limitations; add the README section and the bench section of docs/CLI.md.

objects.title: Performance claims at their proven status
objects.description: Add claims to docs/CLAIMS.yaml for derived benchmark targets, separated cold and warm distributions, flatten-once, cache equivalence and regression refusal, each naming its case, and regenerate the site data.

objects.title: generate-site-data instrumented and its hot spots removed
objects.description: Declare phases per section of the site generator, rank them, and remove the repeated work in the two most expensive sections.

objects.title: knowledge nodes and edges read each source once
objects.description: Time the knowledge stages, then remove the per-file subprocesses in discovery and extraction so that nodes and edges take one pass per source.

objects.title: The test runner reports per-case time and the suite budget
objects.description: Print each case's wall time in test/run.sh, sort the slowest at the end, and record the suite's total in the benchmark history as a system target.

objects.title: CI runs the structural performance checks
objects.description: Add the flatten-once case, the cache-equivalence case and bench --check with the CI profile to validate.yml, with the wall-clock thresholds conservative and the counters exact.

objects.title: A synthetic repository generator for scaling cases
objects.description: Add a test helper that builds a repository with N issues, N milestones, N rules and N context documents from the skeleton, and a case that runs doctor and plan validate at three sizes and asserts the yaml_flatten count grows linearly.

objects.title: Timing report as JSON
objects.description: Under --json, print the timing report as one JSON object on stderr with phases and counters, so bench can carry a phase breakdown per sample.

objects.title: bench compare and the top regressions report
objects.description: Add bench compare <run-a> <run-b> and make the human report rank the largest regressions, the largest improvements and the slowest targets by p95.

objects.title: watch inherits every doctor fix and its own budget
objects.description: Confirm watch dispatches the rewritten validators, time it, and declare benchmark.budget.watch_ms next to doctor's.

objects.title: context and its subcommands under a second
objects.description: Time context resolve, validate, affected and check-sync, and remove the per-document git and awk calls so each runs under a second on this repository.

objects.title: Cache equivalence proved by property-shaped cases
objects.description: For every read-only command in the registry, run it with the cache cold, warm, and disabled, on this repository and on a synthetic one, and assert byte-identical output and exit code; then mutate one file and assert the changed output is served.

objects.title: Before and after evidence for every optimisation
objects.description: Record, for each hot spot removed, the phase time before and after and the counter before and after, in the benchmark history and in the commit message, and summarise them in docs/PERFORMANCE.md by pointing at the baseline file.

objects.title: The performance workflow is discoverable and complete
objects.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion of M004 has evidence, the README workflow runs as written, the site is regenerated, and the final report is a plan record rather than a conversation.

objects.title: The deployment description is a kind of the layer, not a provider file
objects.description: Register `deployment` as a kind of the AI layer — allowed keys, schema, directory contract — and describe this repository's own deployment as one object under .ai/repo/deployments/, so that every later projection reads one file and no provider file is ever authoritative.

objects.title: The deployment object becomes typed Rust that refuses nonsense
objects.description: Parse the canonical deployment object into strongly typed Rust — enums and newtypes rather than strings — and validate it so that a deployment that cannot work is refused before anything is built.

objects.title: Deployment reads are declared once and projected everywhere
objects.description: Declare the read-only deployment operations as canonical capabilities so that the CLI, the HTTP API, MCP, OpenAPI and the generated documentation all derive from one declaration.

objects.title: The listen address is one fact with two projections
objects.description: Make the deployment bind an externally reachable interface on the port the canonical object declares, without changing the loopback default that local use depends on, and without the port existing as a literal in more than one place.

objects.title: Liveness and readiness are registered capabilities, not router hacks
objects.description: Expose cheap liveness and readiness endpoints through the capability registry, so that the provider health check, the container test and the smoke suite all point at routes the registry knows about.

objects.title: Termination is graceful and proved against the real container
objects.description: Handle SIGTERM and SIGINT so that a Machine that is being stopped, redeployed or autostopped finishes its in-flight responses and exits inside the platform's timeout.

objects.title: The running process says what it is, from an allowlist
objects.description: Expose the version, revision, build profile, target and the safe platform facts of a hosted process through the existing metadata surface, with every field explicitly allowlisted.

objects.title: A hosted process has no repository, and says so instead of failing
objects.description: Separate the local mode that inspects a developer's repository from the hosted mode that serves a packaged layer, and report the capabilities that are unavailable in hosted mode from capability metadata rather than from a hand-written list.

objects.title: The production image is a generated projection of the build specification
objects.description: Generate a multi-stage container build and its ignore file from the deployment object's build specification: a pinned Alpine runtime holding the binary, the runtime assets and nothing else, executed by an unprivileged user.

objects.title: The release profile is chosen by measurement, not by folklore
objects.description: Measure the size, startup, memory and latency consequences of the candidate release configurations and select the smallest one that does not regress runtime behaviour materially, recording the decision and the numbers.

objects.title: A source change does not rebuild the world, and the context stays small
objects.description: Make the container build reuse dependency layers and caches so that a source-only change does not rebuild every dependency, and keep the build context to the inputs the deployment object declares.

objects.title: The image serves the site the canonical pipeline produced
objects.description: Build the served documentation and site assets in the container with the same pipeline local development and the Pages deployment already use, and carry exactly those outputs into the runtime stage.

objects.title: The provider configuration is generated, and the cheap profile is declared
objects.description: Generate the Fly configuration from the canonical object — application, region, port, resources, autostart and autostop, health check, concurrency — and declare the cheap cost profile as data that a reader and a check can both see.

objects.title: One deployment core, one command, and a dry run that mutates nothing
objects.description: Implement the deployment operations — validate, plan, generate, build, status, deploy, smoke — once in the typed core, expose them through thin adapters, and provide one ergonomic command that performs the whole sequence safely and can be asked to change nothing.

objects.title: Deployment joins the diagnostics that already exist
objects.description: Add the deployment checks to the health and doctor architecture the repository already has, so that the answer to whether a deployment can succeed comes from the same diagnostic surface as every other verdict.

objects.title: The smoke suite is derived from the route registry, never written twice
objects.description: Generate the deployment smoke tests from the authoritative route registry, extending route metadata only where smoke testing genuinely needs it, and cover the surfaces that a plain status code cannot verify.

objects.title: A bad deployment can be undone deterministically
objects.description: Record the deployed image reference before changing production and provide a rollback that rests on what the provider actually supports, so that a failed smoke run has an exit.

objects.title: The bootstrap credential is used once and belongs to nothing
objects.description: Define and implement how a deployment credential is discovered for an interactive first deployment, so that it is consumed in one process, never persisted, and leaves no trace of where it came from.

objects.title: Nothing secret and nothing local leaves in the image
objects.description: Automate the verification that no credential material and no developer path appears in the image, its metadata, the generated artifacts, the site output, the API documents or the deployment report.

objects.title: The image's dependencies are known and its advisories are policy
objects.description: Record what the production image contains, obtain a dependency audit and a vulnerability verdict, and state a severity and fix-availability policy so that the gate is meaningful rather than permanently red.

objects.title: Size is measured first and budgeted second
objects.description: Measure the binary, the assets, the image and the build context, declare budgets with headroom over the measured baseline, and gate unexplained growth.

objects.title: The memory hypothesis is tested, not asserted
objects.description: Run the production image under the intended memory limit, measure resident memory through a representative request sequence, and let the evidence decide the memory the deployment declares.

objects.title: Cold start and endpoint cost are benchmark targets like everything else
objects.description: Measure the cold start of the container and the cost of the cheap endpoints through the benchmark infrastructure the repository already has, and record them as baselines.

objects.title: The decision is recorded where architecture decisions are recorded
objects.description: Write the architecture decision record for deploying as a generated projection of canonical deployment metadata, with the alternatives that were genuinely considered and the consequences that follow.

objects.title: Every deployment rule is a check that runs
objects.description: State the durable deployment constraints as project rules in the repository's rule system, and give each one an executable check that CI runs.

objects.title: The deployment documentation is generated and reachable
objects.description: Produce the deployment documentation from the canonical object and the implementation — architecture, container, resources, workflow, CI, security, cost, troubleshooting and scaling — and make it reachable from the surfaces that are already generated.

objects.title: The cockpit shows the deployment from the same data
objects.description: Add a deployment view to the existing cockpit that reads static policy from the canonical object and live facts from the running process, using the projection the cockpit already is.

objects.title: A pull request cannot merge a deployment that would not work
objects.description: Extend the existing verification workflow so that a pull request runs the deployment validation, the projection drift check, the production image build, the container smoke run, the resource policy assertions and the security checks.

objects.title: Production deploys from CI with a token scoped to one application
objects.description: Deploy production from CI on the repository's existing branch policy, using an application-scoped deploy token rather than an account-wide one, with concurrency that stops two pushes racing the same application.

objects.title: The real image runs under the real limits before anything is deployed
objects.description: Build the actual production image and run it under the resource limits of the cheap profile, verifying the process, its user, its port and its routes without fixed ports and without sleeping.

objects.title: The application exists, one machine runs it, and the URL answers
objects.description: Create or resolve the production application, deploy the cheap profile without accidental redundancy, verify the machine inventory and the resources against the declared policy, run the route-derived smoke suite against the public URL, and write the deployment report.

objects.title: The milestone is accepted on its evidence
objects.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measured baselines are documented with the environment they were taken on, the workflow in the documentation runs as written, and the outcome is a plan record rather than a conversation.

objects.title: One typed graph composes the registries that already own their facts
objects.description: Extend the executable's graph derivation into a typed, deterministic model that composes the existing authoritative registries — capabilities, commands, routes, MCP exposure, skills, rules, decisions, documents, use cases, benchmarks — without any of them ceasing to be authoritative.

objects.title: Relations are typed, inferred from stable identities, and never dangle
objects.description: Give the graph typed relations — implements, documents, exposes, generated from, enforced by, tested by, benchmarked by, depends on, projects to, served at — inferred where a stable convention exists, declared where it does not, and resolved or refused.

objects.title: Skills, rules, decisions, documents, use cases and benchmarks enter the graph as themselves
objects.description: Bring the layer's own kinds into the graph through the registries that already index them, so that a rule, a skill, a decision, a document, a use case, a benchmark and a deployment are navigable next to the capabilities they govern.

objects.title: Availability and visibility are metadata, not conditions in a template
objects.description: Model where a capability is available — always, only in a static build, only with a running backend, only when authenticated, only at build time — and whether it is public or internal, so that every surface derives its behaviour from that rather than from its own conditionals.

objects.title: The graph is a generated artifact with a schema and no unsafe field
objects.description: Serialise the graph as a deterministic generated artifact with a schema, carrying safe metadata only, produced by the generation the repository already runs.

objects.title: The runtime reads the graph through the registry, like every other read
objects.description: Expose the graph to the running Cockpit as a declared capability, so that its route, its schema, its documentation and its benchmark coverage all follow from the declaration.

objects.title: The site renders the same graph, generated once
objects.description: Produce the static projection of the graph through the existing generation and site pipeline, so that the published site renders the same model the server does without a backend and without a second generator.

objects.title: The two projections are proved to be the same model
objects.description: Test that the static and runtime representations of the graph are equal once runtime-only fields are removed, so the published site and the running server cannot become alternate realities.

objects.title: Every menu in this repository comes from one derivation
objects.description: Derive the desktop navigation, the mobile navigation, the Cockpit sections, the documentation navigation and the landing links from one projection of the graph, with deterministic grouping and ordering.

objects.title: The overview is what exists, counted rather than claimed
objects.description: Generate the Cockpit overview and its summary numbers from the graph, showing a section only when the repository actually holds that kind of thing.

objects.title: The coverage matrix reports evidence, and never a green cell without one
objects.description: Generate a matrix showing, for every capability, whether it is documented, tested, enforced, benchmarked and exposed, where each cell resolves to an artifact or a relation rather than to a claim.

objects.title: One detail view, assembled from what a node actually has
objects.description: Render a capability's detail page from its populated sections and its resolved relations, with a stable deep link and a repository-relative reference to where the information came from.

objects.title: Search over the graph, generated, with nothing to run
objects.description: Provide one search over identities, titles, descriptions, tags, categories, commands, routes and documents, from a generated index that works in the static build with no service behind it.

objects.title: The relation view reads the graph and holds no data of its own
objects.description: Render the relation graph interactively from the generated data, with filters, focus, neighbour highlighting and deep links, loaded only where it is used and bounded in cost.

objects.title: A surface with no server behind it is not offered as if it had one
objects.description: Make the exposure of backend-only surfaces — the API console, live status, runtime reads — follow from availability metadata, and prove both projections behave correctly.

objects.title: The Cockpit works on a phone and before JavaScript runs
objects.description: Make the Cockpit genuinely usable at narrow viewports and keep its core information present in the served HTML, with JavaScript adding filtering, the graph, live state and search rather than being required to read anything.

objects.title: Live state is an overlay that degrades to nothing
objects.description: Let the running Cockpit overlay live state — health, peers, runtime metrics, deployment status — over the same graph, through the transport the process already has, degrading cleanly where there is none.

objects.title: The surface rules exist as checks, proved by making them fail
objects.description: State the durable constraints of this architecture as project rules with executable checks: derived surfaces stay synchronised, a public capability is discoverable, a behavioural capability carries verification, a developer-facing capability resolves to documentation, and the two projections stay equal.

objects.title: One skill runs the whole loop, and is itself in the graph
objects.description: Provide a skill that discovers capabilities, validates the graph, reports what is missing documentation, tests, exposure or enforcement, regenerates the projections and reports drift — registered, documented, tested and visible like any other.

objects.title: The graph's health is answered by the doctor that already answers everything else
objects.description: Add the graph's diagnostics to the existing health and doctor surface: the graph builds, identities are unique, relations resolve, projections are synchronised, required documentation and verification are present, and nothing unsafe is exposed.

objects.title: A browser proves the interface, at the widths people use
objects.description: Extend the existing browser checking to cover navigation on desktop and mobile, search and filtering, the detail view, graph initialisation, conditional runtime exposure, link integrity and console errors.

objects.title: Drift in any derived surface fails the build
objects.description: Extend the generation check to cover every artifact this milestone introduces — the graph, the static projection, the navigation, the indexes, the search data — so a stale committed projection cannot merge.

objects.title: Nothing private reaches a published page
objects.description: Scan the published graph, the static site and everything the client receives for credential material, private environment values and machine-absolute paths, and fail on a finding without printing it.

objects.title: The interface has a weight, and it is measured
objects.description: Measure the generated data, the served HTML, the initial scripts and styles and the graph's initialisation, and hold them to budgets through the benchmark infrastructure the repository already has.

objects.title: The federated model and its two projections are an architecture decision
objects.description: Record the decision to compose the authoritative registries into one typed graph and to render it as two projections, with the alternatives that were real and the consequences that follow.

objects.title: The architecture explains itself, from inside itself
objects.description: Document the graph, its sources, its relation model, its two projections and the contributor workflow, and let the interface say how it was generated and from what.

objects.title: A synthetic capability proves the architecture instead of describing it
objects.description: Register a synthetic capability at its authoritative source alone, and prove it reaches the graph, the interface, the search, the navigation and the static projection with no other edit — and that omitting its required evidence fails enforcement.

objects.title: The inventories this replaces are removed, not left running beside it
objects.description: Find the hand-maintained inventories this architecture replaces — menus, landing cards, route lists, documentation indexes, rule and skill catalogues — and remove them, so that one derivation is the only one.

objects.title: The gate refuses what would silently break the interface
objects.description: Put the drift check, the enforcement rules, the parity test, the browser checks and the public-data scan into the existing verification workflow, so that a change leaving any derived surface stale or unsafe cannot merge.

objects.title: The milestone is accepted on its evidence
objects.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measurements are recorded with their environment, the contributor workflow runs as written, and the remaining gaps are stated.

objects.title: A served surface says which checkout it is serving
objects.description: Make every surface a process serves name the repository it is serving — its root and its identity — so that a reader can tell at a glance whether the answers in front of them come from the tree they are working in.

objects.title: What this tool leaves behind, established by inspection rather than by memory
objects.description: Establish, from the repository rather than from recollection, every path Majordomus writes, generates or mutates when a project adopts it — where each lands, which subsystem writes it, whether anything records it, and which are canonical, derived or accidental.

objects.title: The two namespaces are a typed contract, not a habit
objects.description: Declare the canonical layout of `.ai/` and `.majordomus/` as typed, versioned data — what each namespace holds, what it must never hold, and which lifecycle each directory's contents carry — so that the boundary can be checked rather than remembered.

objects.title: Whether a file is authored or derived is a field, not a naming convention
objects.description: Give every machine-processable artifact an explicit provenance and lifecycle — authored, derived, generated, cache or runtime — with its generator, its inputs and whether it is disposable, so that no consumer has to infer from a path what a file is.

objects.title: Both namespaces carry their contracts, all the way down
objects.description: Extend the directory-contract discipline that already governs `.ai/` to `.majordomus/`, so every directory of either namespace explains its purpose, its ownership, its lifecycle, the schemas that apply and how its contents are discovered.

objects.title: The repository is discovered once, into one model
objects.description: Build the one typed model of a repository — identity, structure, capabilities, the layer's registries, workflows, environments, providers, services and version-control state — discovered once and read by every consumer.

objects.title: The registries are views of the model, not separate discoveries
objects.description: Make the typed registries — skills, rules, decisions, workflows, use cases, providers, capabilities — views over the one repository model, so that adding a valid artifact under a discoverable namespace registers it everywhere with no second edit.

objects.title: Discovery is deterministic, cached, and its cost is known
objects.description: Make one discovery over one tree produce one answer, cache it by what it was derived from, and measure what it costs — because everything downstream now pays that cost.

objects.title: The desired integration is a value, and the plan is a diff
objects.description: Compute what a repository's Majordomus integration should look like as a typed value, diff it against what the repository actually holds, and make the apply the smallest mutation that closes the gap.

objects.title: Everything placed outside the two namespaces is recorded, with what it was
objects.description: Record every mutation Majordomus makes outside `.ai/` and `.majordomus/` in a typed ledger: the path, the kind of mutation, the content hash as written, the generator and version that wrote it, and what was there before.

objects.title: The second run changes nothing, and a test says so
objects.description: Make reconciliation idempotent: running it against a conforming repository produces no change at all, and prove it with a test rather than with an observation.

objects.title: Uninstall gives back exactly what was taken
objects.description: Implement removal that reverses every recorded mutation, refuses anything a person has since edited, and leaves authored knowledge in place unless removal is asked for separately and explicitly.

objects.title: What touches the root is two small blocks, and they never change again
objects.description: Reduce every root-level integration to a small, stable, machine-owned bridge: a managed block in the agent document that points at the layer, and — when direnv is wanted — one line that sources the environment integration.

objects.title: Entering a directory is local, bounded and silent about the network
objects.description: Keep environment entry — the direnv hook, the banner, the shell integration — local, bounded and free of build and network work, and measure it against a declared budget.

objects.title: A provider is an adapter over the model, and adding one is an implementation
objects.description: Make every provider-specific representation a derived adapter over the repository model, so that supporting another provider is one implementation rather than a copy of the instructions in another file.

objects.title: Completion comes from the command model, not from a second list
objects.description: Derive shell completion from the same command model the CLI and its documentation already come from, so that a new command is completable without anything being listed.

objects.title: This repository's own footprint moves, through the reconciler
objects.description: Migrate what this repository itself scatters — root scripts, provider files, configuration beside configuration, generated state outside the namespaces — into `.ai/` and `.majordomus/`, using the reconciler and its migrations rather than a move script.

objects.title: The hand-maintained lists are removed, not left running beside the derivation
objects.description: Find every list that enumerates what discovery already finds — indexes, menus, route tables, provider lists, documentation catalogues — and remove it, so that one derivation is the only one.

objects.title: Every invariant of this milestone is a rule with a check that runs
objects.description: Turn the invariants — bounded footprint, no manual registration, disposable derived artifacts, reversible managed mutations, idempotent reconciliation, root files as adapters, zero-registration extension — into project rules, each with an executable check that CI runs and a negative test that proves it fires.

objects.title: The budgets are measured, and a regression fails rather than being noticed
objects.description: Measure what this architecture costs — discovery, reconciliation, the environment entry, the generated artifacts — and hold each to a budget derived from its measured baseline.

objects.title: A refusal says what to do about it
objects.description: Make every refusal in this subsystem name the source of truth, what was observed, what was expected and the command that repairs it — through the diagnostics framework that already exists.

objects.title: Every surface shows the integration from the one model
objects.description: Project the integration state — what is adopted, what is owned, what is generated, what would change — through the CLI, the API and its document, MCP, the Cockpit and the documentation, from the one model and with no parallel definition.

objects.title: A foreign repository, adopted, upgraded and given back
objects.description: Prove the contract against a repository that is not this one: adopt it, verify the footprint, run it again, upgrade the tool, edit a bridge by hand, then remove the adoption and compare what is left against what was there before.

objects.title: The milestone is accepted on its evidence
objects.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measured baselines are recorded with the environment they were taken on, the adoption and removal run as documented on a clean checkout, and the remaining limitations are stated.

objects.title: An identity provider is a declarative object, and Google and Facebook are two of them
objects.description: Introduce the identity-provider kind: a JSON Schema, an entry in share/kinds.yaml, the generated allow-list, a directory contract under .ai/repo/identity/providers/, and the first two objects — google and facebook — each stating its issuer, its endpoints or discovery document, the scopes it is asked for, the claim that carries a stable subject, the environment variable names its client id and client secret arrive in, its display name and its order in the sign-in offer.

objects.title: One typed provider model reads the objects, and no code names a provider
objects.description: Add apps/majordomus-cli/src/identity with the typed model of a provider object: discovery of every object under .ai/repo/identity/providers/, validation against the schema, resolution of the credential environment variables at use rather than at load, and a deterministic ordering of the sign-in offer. Expose the read as a capability so the provider list reaches the CLI, the API, OpenAPI, MCP and the Cockpit through the registry rather than through five readers.

objects.title: One flow serves every provider, and it refuses everything it did not start
objects.description: Implement the authorisation-code flow with PKCE once, over the typed provider model: a start route that issues state and nonce and redirects to the provider's authorisation endpoint, a callback route that refuses a state it did not issue or that has expired, exchanges the code, verifies the issuer, the audience, the expiry and the nonce of the returned identity token, and resolves the stable subject from the claim the object names.

objects.title: The session is signed, short, and revocable from the server
objects.description: Issue the session as a signed cookie carrying an opaque identifier, keep the server-side record needed to revoke it, set HttpOnly, SameSite and Secure according to how the surface is served, expire it, and implement sign-out as a server-side revocation rather than a cleared cookie.

objects.title: Identity is resolved once, in the router, and every surface reads it from there
objects.description: Resolve the caller once, where the request enters, and carry the result to every surface: the HTTP API, the Cockpit's rendering, the OpenAPI document's security scheme and the MCP surface. No handler parses a cookie, and no surface decides for itself what an absent identity means.

objects.title: What an anonymous reader may do is derived from the effect classification, not from a list
objects.description: Derive the exposure decision from the capability registry: a read-only capability stays open to an anonymous reader, anything that mutates requires an identified one, and the decision is stated once in policy over effect classes rather than per route. Project the decision into the OpenAPI security scheme, the Cockpit's disabled controls with their reason, and the generated documentation.

objects.title: No credential reaches any output, and hostile provider metadata renders safely
objects.description: Prove the negatives. Place sentinel values in the client-secret and signing-key environment variables and exercise every output this repository produces — API responses, the Cockpit's HTML, the generated site, OpenAPI and its examples, MCP answers, the artifact manifest, the caches, the logs and the doctor report — asserting no sentinel appears anywhere. Separately, give a provider object a display name carrying control characters, ANSI sequences and markup, and assert it renders as text in the terminal, in the HTML and in the JSON.

objects.title: Adding a provider is one file, removing one is one deletion, and both are executed rather than described
objects.description: Document how a provider is added and how one is struck, and make the documentation executable: a test that adds a synthetic provider object and asserts it appears in the sign-in offer, in the capability read, in the generated documentation and in the Cockpit with no other edit, and a test that removes one of the two shipped objects and asserts every one of those surfaces loses it.

objects.title: A workspace is a declared object of the layer; only its content is local
objects.description: Register `workspace` as a kind — allowed keys, schema, directory contract — and declare the first workspace under .ai/repo/workspaces/, so that the catalogue of what may be synced is the repository's own tracked statement while the synced content stays out of the tracked tree.

objects.title: Identity, provenance and support level are typed fields, not prose
objects.description: Define the record model every synced item carries: upstream identity, local identity, content hash, the transport that produced it, the acquisition mode, the support level and the tombstone, as a schema with a version, before any adapter writes a byte.

objects.title: The store is bounded, measured and invisible to every published projection
objects.description: Declare the layout of .ai/local/workspaces/, its checkpoint file, its retention cap in policy and the doctor stanza that measures it, and prove with a gate that nothing published ever reaches it.

objects.title: The browser transport is the one this repository already drives
objects.description: Implement the authenticated browser transport in the Node tooling layer beside scripts/lib/ui-audit.mjs: Playwright over the system Chrome, an explicitly named profile, observation scoped to the vendor's own origins, and sanitisation before anything is persisted.

objects.title: An observed contract has a fingerprint, a compatibility state and a fixture
objects.description: Record what the browser observed as a versioned contract: a fingerprint of the shape, a compatibility state, and a sanitised fixture that CI replays — so that a private surface changing is a diagnosable event rather than a silent wrong answer.

objects.title: A sync resumes, repeats itself without harm, and says how fresh it is
objects.description: Implement the sync: incremental from a durable checkpoint, idempotent on replay, bounded in what one run may fetch, and honest about how each change was acquired.

objects.title: The ChatGPT shape is mapped from evidence and never becomes the canonical model
objects.description: Map what a ChatGPT Project actually exposes — the project, its conversations, the message graph, content parts, attachment metadata, project instructions — onto the canonical record model, mapping only what an observation supports.

objects.title: The executable's share is one capability, shaped like continuity
objects.description: Add one capability to majordomus-cli that reads the store and reports what is declared, what is synced, how fresh each workspace is and at what support level — served, never published, with no site or documentation projection.

objects.title: The boundaries this milestone asserts are gates, not sentences
objects.description: Add the gates that make ADR 0025 enforceable: the dependency boundary of majordomus-cli, the credential leak check over the store and the fixtures, the retention cap, and the publication boundary.

objects.title: The subsystem is documented where a person looks, and the plan is closed against the repository
objects.description: Write docs/WORKSPACES.md, add the row to the documentation index, and re-audit the repository against this milestone: what was reinvented, what legacy duplication survives, and which of the pack's phases turned out not to apply here.

objects.title: The identity of a projected record is what the record carries, not what its title says
objects.description: Make the adapter find a remote record by an identity the record itself carries, so that a person may rename an issue on GitHub without the projection losing it or creating a second one, and make reconciliation provable without a network.

objects.title: A finding says which of six states it found, and the state that could hide a person's edit is no longer one of them
objects.description: Derive a typed state for every projected record from two independent questions — has a person rewritten the generated region since it was posted, and has the canonical record moved since — and report the answer instead of collapsing both into one word.

objects.title: Backfill the projection once, deliberately, and record what it created
objects.description: Apply the projection so that every canonical record exists on GitHub exactly once, adopt the 19 records that already exist rather than duplicating them, and record the run as evidence.

objects.title: The drift check is a gate, so a projection that stops being applied cannot stay silent
objects.description: Run `scripts/github-sync --check` from CI on every change that can move the canonical model or the adapter, and fail the build on drift with the record and the remedy named.

objects.title: A pull request names the issue it realises, and the edge is derived rather than remembered
objects.description: Derive the relation between an issue and the pull requests, branches and commits that realised it, from git and from GitHub, and make it traversable in both directions.

objects.title: The plan's derivations are capabilities, so every surface reads the readiness the terminal reads
objects.description: Make status, ready, blocked, waves, next and roadmap answerable through the capability registry, so that MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI and the Cockpit read the derived plan rather than only the raw documents.

objects.title: One issue travels the whole path and back, as an executable case
objects.description: Prove the milestone with a case that carries one synthetic issue from outcome to accepted completion and then traverses the same chain backwards, offline, against fixtures.

objects.title: The documents stop claiming a projection nobody runs
objects.description: Bring the prose in line with what the gates prove, and keep it there by citing the gate rather than the intention.

objects.title: Derived data stops hashing inputs it cannot control
objects.description: Make a committed derivation describe something it can be a projection of, and put the staleness refusal where merges actually happen.

objects.title: An execution a person starts is an execution the server can see
objects.description: Make `majordomus-cli run` reach the server that serves this repository, so that the execution plane a surface shows and the execution plane a person uses are the same plane — or record the decision that they are not, and stop every surface from implying otherwise.

objects.title: A server serving code that no longer exists stops calling itself ready
objects.description: Make a running server's own root and health documents carry the identity of the code it is serving, so that a stale server is detectable by the client reading it rather than only by an outside reader holding a newer executable.

objects.title: A closed session is not closed a second time under the same identity
objects.description: Stop the session closer from writing a second record for a session that already has one, so that a session identity names one record and the index does not exclude every claimant of it.

objects.title: One development transition is a capability, end to end
objects.description: Declare one development transition — the plan's `done` — as a single `capability!` of kind command in the plan module, with a typed input schema, benchmark cases and a registered ledger event, and point lib/plan.sh at it instead of letting it write the YAML itself.

objects.title: A mutating capability leaves a durable event, and the ledger can be read back
objects.description: Give a capability of kind command one way to record what it did: append a ledger event whose name share/events.yaml declares, publish the same change to the execution stream, and add a read capability for the ledger so a surface can show history at all.

objects.title: The lifecycle commands become non-interactive capabilities
objects.description: Move task start, checkpoint and finish, session open and close, handover and evidence into the pattern Phase A establishes, each one non-interactive, so that the exposure policy stops withholding them from every machine surface.

objects.title: Issues, milestones, sessions and peers reach the Cockpit as projections
objects.description: Give the Cockpit the development areas it has none of — issues, milestones, sessions, peers and the current task — each one rendering what a capability answered and computing nothing of its own.

objects.title: The navigation is derived from the dispatcher, not kept beside it
objects.description: Reconcile the Cockpit's area list against the routes the dispatcher actually answers, and derive or check the route table in docs/COCKPIT.md, so that a routed page cannot be invisible.

objects.title: A detail page that pages nothing has outgrown the reason it pages nothing
objects.description: Reconcile the two things the Cockpit's largest page is trying to be — complete before any JavaScript loads, and usable by a person — without giving up the first, and bring the page under the test sweep that covers every other one.

objects.title: A gap the audit calls planned names a plan object that exists
objects.description: Check docs/COCKPIT_IDE_AUDIT.md's gap matrix against the plan, so that a row whose status is `planned` must name an issue that exists, and a row cannot quietly claim to be scheduled when nothing schedules it.

objects.title: The documentation surface answers in a checkout that has not built the site
objects.description: Make /docs/ say what it needs rather than fail, so that a developer entering a fresh worktree does not meet a broken documentation surface as their first impression of the runtime.

objects.title: Gate state is something the runtime can answer
objects.description: Give the runtime a capability that answers what the repository's gates are and how the last run of each one went, so that CI status stops being the one observability subject with no reader on any surface.

objects.title: One completion policy, a derived stage, and live verification of what was deployed
objects.description: Make share/completion.yaml the one definition of done, derive the lifecycle stage and the complete bit from the answers to it, refuse the outcome completed until the bit is true, verify the published site, the release metadata and every active deployment against what the trunk expects, put the structural version gate on the release path, and render the definition of done into every provider bootstrap from the policy rather than by hand.

objects.title: The documents that explain this repository are read in a fixed order
objects.description: What to read before changing this repository, and which document answers which question.

objects.title: Milestone and DAG driven development
objects.description: Every non-trivial change in this repository belongs to a milestone specification and to one dependency-linked issue execution contract, validated as a DAG, with status derived rather than asserted, and projected to GitHub and to the website from that one canonical model.

objects.title: A blocking question survives a handover
objects.description: An unresolved question keeps refusing a completed finish after the work moves to a new task, or the alternative is chosen deliberately and the reason is recorded where the next worker will read it.

objects.title: A durable record names the worker that wrote it
objects.description: A durable record either names the worker that produced it or is refused, and a record written from one session can never arrive attributed to another session's task.

objects.title: A session is a durable envelope, and knowledge is compiled from what is already canonical
objects.description: A worker with no conversation history can answer what happened, why, what was decided, which evidence supports it, where the canonical source lives, and what to do next — from records and a derived index, with git still the authority over both.

objects.title: Performance is executable evidence, and the hot path does no canonical work twice
objects.description: Every public command can be benchmarked from the command registry with cold and warm distributions, the phases and work counters of any run can be printed, the caches and batch reads that remove repeated work preserve every observable result, an accepted baseline lives in the repository and a check refuses a regression by policy, and the pre-commit hook is fast enough that nobody routes around it.

objects.title: One capability graph, two projections, and no second inventory of what this repository can do
objects.description: One typed, deterministic capability graph composes the registries that already own their facts — it does not replace them — and adds typed relations between them that are inferred where a stable convention exists and declared where it does not. Both the running server and the published site render from that one graph: the static projection is the snapshot, the runtime projection is the snapshot plus live state. Navigation, overview, detail, search, the relation view and the coverage matrix are all derived, a dangling relation fails generation rather than rendering as a missing section, and a capability that exists with no documentation, no test or no enforcement is visible as such rather than indistinguishable from one that has them.

objects.title: A development session is complete when the repository can prove it, and every surface reads the same proof
objects.description: One completion policy, share/completion.yaml, is the definition of done. The completion report derives the lifecycle stage a task stands at from the answers to it, states whether the task is complete, and every surface - check and finish, the HTTP route, the MCP tool, the Cockpit, the generated section of every provider bootstrap, the site - reads that one report. The outcome completed is refused until the report says complete. The published site, the release metadata and every active deployment are asked what they serve and compared with what the trunk expects, and a stale or unreachable surface refuses. The release path runs the structural version gate.

objects.title: Cost per accepted outcome, only on measured data
objects.description: The cost of an accepted outcome is computed from measured telemetry and the finish contract that accepted it, and is reported only where both exist.

objects.title: A committed derivation describes something it can be a projection of
objects.description: A committed derived artifact is a projection of inputs the commit owns. Landing an unrelated change on the trunk does not invalidate it, a fixture whose object database has no history can still evaluate it, and the staleness refusal exists on the path merges actually take - so the first thing that says no is a check rather than the published site.

objects.title: The runtime has a development surface
objects.description: A development transition is decided in exactly one place — a `capability!` of kind `command` in the Rust registry — and every surface that offers it is a projection: the CLI, the MCP tool, the HTTP route, the OpenAPI operation and the Cockpit's generated runner form, none of them written by hand. The lifecycle stops being a second program with no surfaces, and the execution history a development surface would show exists somewhere durable.

objects.title: Execution telemetry, only from providers that expose it honestly
objects.description: Execution telemetry is recorded for providers that report it truthfully, and absence is recorded as absence rather than estimated.

objects.title: An external workspace is read the way this repository reads anything else, and its content never becomes public by accident
objects.description: A workspace is a declared object of the layer — vendor, identity, what the operator authorised, which browser profile reaches it, which capabilities it is expected to have — and rides the existing kind pipeline onto every surface with no code that special-cases it. Its content is synced by the Node tooling layer that already drives the system browser, lands under `.ai/local/workspaces/`, carries provenance and a support level on every record, and is read back through exactly one capability shaped like `continuity`: served, never published. A sync is incremental from a durable checkpoint, idempotent on replay, fails closed when an observed contract breaks, and never writes a credential anywhere.

objects.title: A deployment is a projection of the repository model, and a reachable URL is its evidence
objects.description: One canonical deployment object under .ai/repo/deployments/ describes the deployment; a typed Rust model parses and validates it; the container image, the Fly configuration, the smoke suite, the doctor checks, the documentation, the cockpit view and the CI jobs are all projections of that object and of the capability registry, and every one of them is checked for drift. The service runs on Fly.io on a single shared-CPU Machine that stops when idle, its health and readiness are verified from outside, the smoke suite is derived from the route registry rather than written twice, and the deployed URL answers.

objects.title: A supervisory control layer that is real rather than described
objects.description: A repository carries one policy, a small set of profiles, durable task state, and a set of commands that refuse work which does not meet a declared contract — with every rule dispatched from a registry that proves it reaches the command claiming to run it.

objects.title: Routing recommendations derived from measured cost
objects.description: The profile a task should run under is recommended from measured cost per accepted outcome, and the recommendation names the data it came from.

objects.title: Profiles become runtime constraints rather than advice
objects.description: A profile's axes become opt-in runtime clamps a provider actually applies — read size, output condensation, subagent budget — with the limit derived from the profile rather than configured twice.

objects.title: Shared policy across repositories and workers
objects.description: A policy can be shared across repositories and workers, with local override remaining explicit and drift from the shared source detectable in one command.

objects.title: A repository that adopts Majordomus gains two directories and two lines, and can give them back
objects.description: Adoption is a reconciliation, not a template copy. One typed repository model is discovered once and every consumer reads it. A desired integration is computed from that model, diffed against what the repository actually holds, and applied as the smallest mutation that closes the gap — with everything Majordomus owns living under `.ai/` and `.majordomus/`, and anything outside those two namespaces reduced to a small managed bridge whose ownership is recorded. Running the reconciliation twice changes nothing the second time, and uninstalling gives back exactly what was taken and nothing a person authored.

objects.title: The deployed surfaces know who is asking, and the identity providers are data
objects.description: One canonical identity-provider kind under .ai/repo/identity/providers/ describes each provider as data: its issuer, its endpoints or its discovery document, the scopes requested, the claim that carries a stable subject and the environment variable names its credentials arrive in. A single OpenID-Connect-shaped flow in the executable serves every provider in that directory; Google and Facebook are two objects, not two code paths. Sessions are cookie-borne, signed, short and revocable; identity is attached to a request once, in the router, and every surface — HTTP, Cockpit, OpenAPI, MCP — reads it from the same place. The capability registry's effect classification, not a per-route list, decides what an anonymous reader may do, and the OpenAPI document and the Cockpit both state that decision because both project it from the registry. Striking a provider is deleting one file and regenerating.

objects.title: The projection to GitHub is gated, identified and traversable, and a merged pull request leads back to the outcome it served
objects.description: The projection cannot rot silently: a gate runs the drift check on every change that can move the model or the adapter, and drift is a CI failure with the record named. Identity travels with the record rather than being parsed out of its title, so renaming a GitHub title moves nothing and creates no duplicate, and the remote can be a fixture, so which record is which is provable with no network. The reconciliation vocabulary distinguishes the states it currently conflates, so `missing` no longer stands for both a record never created and a record a person deleted, and a remote edit is reported as a remote edit. Above the projection, a pull request names the issue it realises and the edge is derived from git and GitHub rather than remembered, so a merged commit leads back to the acceptance criteria it satisfied and an outcome leads forward to the evidence that it holds. The derivations the shell already computes — ready, blocked, waves, next, status — are readable through the same capability surface as every other thing this repository knows, rather than only from a terminal.

objects.title: A worktree nobody can decide to delete
objects.description: Isolation is cheap to create and expensive to reason about: nothing records what a worktree was for or whether its work landed.

objects.title: The interface changed and its contract document did not
objects.description: A contract maintained by hand beside the code it describes goes stale on the first change that forgets it.

objects.title: A change that no plan ever asked for
objects.description: Work arrives with no bounded contract behind it, so its scope, its acceptance criteria and its ownership are all decided after the fact.

objects.title: The instruction file that grew into a rulebook
objects.description: Everything important gets appended to the always-loaded file, so every session pays for every rule and reads none of them carefully.

objects.title: A fluent contribution that could not have known the rules
objects.description: Assistants let anybody produce plausible contributions at volume; the conventions that make one correct are still only in the maintainers.

objects.title: The decision exists, in a conversation nobody can find
objects.description: A decision that was reached in a session is stored where only that session can read it, so it is neither reviewable nor discoverable.

objects.title: A hard-won discovery that never became knowledge
objects.description: A worker learns something expensive about the codebase, uses it once, and it dies with the session because nothing turned it into a durable record.

objects.title: The documented command that no longer works
objects.description: Examples are written once, in prose, and nothing ever executes them again.

objects.title: Accepting "done" because the model said so
objects.description: A fluent completion claim is accepted as evidence because nothing wrote down, beforehand, what would have to be true.

objects.title: A rule enforced by a hook that never runs
objects.description: Every artefact of enforcement exists — the rule, the script, the test — and no path connects them, so the control is fiction.

objects.title: A failure that was seen once and never again
objects.description: A failure observed inside a session is described in that session and nowhere else, so the next one starts from the report rather than the evidence.

objects.title: A capability the documentation promises and nothing proves
objects.description: A sentence describing what the software does is written once and never connected to anything that would fail if it stopped being true.

objects.title: The first hour in a repository nobody can explain quickly
objects.description: What is conventional in a codebase is knowledge held by its regulars, so every arrival — human or machine — pays for it again.

objects.title: Green tests over stale generated files
objects.description: Tests exercise the code and say nothing about the committed outputs derived from it, so the build is green and the artifacts are wrong.

objects.title: Code that quietly contradicts a written decision
objects.description: The decision was recorded and the implementation went the other way, because nothing relates a decision to the paths it governs.

objects.title: The issue says done and the repository disagrees
objects.description: Completion is recorded as a state change in a tracker rather than as evidence in the repository, so the two drift immediately.

objects.title: Nobody can reconstruct where the milestone actually is
objects.description: Progress is an aggregate that exists only in people, because the parts it aggregates were never recorded in a form anything can add up.

objects.title: Nobody can say why that worker was chosen
objects.description: Provider and model selection is made implicitly, per session, and recorded nowhere, so it cannot be reviewed or repeated.

objects.title: One worker undoing another worker's change
objects.description: A worker sees an unexplained change in its path, judges it wrong, and removes it — correctly, on the evidence it had.

objects.title: The policy changed and its four copies did not
objects.description: A decision is updated at its source and the generated copies keep serving the previous version, with nothing reporting the difference.

objects.title: Re-arguing a decision that was settled last week
objects.description: A decision whose reason lived in a conversation cannot be reviewed, only re-argued — by a worker with less information than the first one had.

objects.title: Re-explaining the same context to a brand-new session
objects.description: Repository knowledge that only ever existed in a conversation has to be re-transmitted by hand to every worker that follows.

objects.title: A result nobody can reproduce, including its author
objects.description: The result is recorded and the conditions that produced it are not, so it is an anecdote rather than a measurement.

objects.title: The rule for that directory, in a README no session ever loaded
objects.description: A local rule is either in the always-loaded file, where every session pays for it, or beside the code, where nothing relates it to the path being edited.

objects.title: The same dead end, explored twice
objects.description: Negative results are the majority of experimental output and the part nobody records, so the search space is re-explored.

objects.title: Two sessions in one checkout, standing on each other
objects.description: Two workers in one working tree see each other only as unexplained file changes, and each treats the other as noise.

objects.title: A public page promising something nothing tests
objects.description: Public material is written by a different act from the code, so it drifts ahead of the behaviour and nothing brings it back.

objects.title: Spend that cannot be tied to anything accepted
objects.description: Consumption is measured per account and outcomes are recorded per person, so the two can never be joined.

objects.title: The strongest model, at maximum effort, renaming a variable
objects.description: Capability, reasoning depth, context size and verbosity collapse into one habit — everything on — because nothing ever named them separately.

objects.title: A task "in progress" that nobody has touched for three weeks
objects.description: A status that was authored rather than computed is true at the moment of writing and decays silently from then on.

objects.title: Three copies of one explanation, and no way to tell which is current
objects.description: Every hand-maintained copy of a fact drifts on its own schedule, and a reader cannot tell which copy is the current one.

objects.title: Three roadmaps, and none of them true
objects.description: A plan kept in prose is a snapshot, and every copy of it drifts on its own schedule; stored status is an assertion that stays true after the world moves.

objects.title: Two agents fixing the same bug in two branches
objects.description: Two workers spend a day each on one defect because ownership was implicit and neither could see the other.

objects.title: Two different rulebooks for one repository
objects.description: Each provider reads its own hand-edited file, nothing relates them, and which contract applies depends on which tool is open.

objects.title: A cheap worker deciding something expensive
objects.description: Capability is dialled down for cost and nothing distinguishes the tasks where that is prudent from the ones where it is expensive.

objects.title: Asking what the workers did last night, and getting a transcript
objects.description: A conversation log records what was said, not what happened, so the operational question has to be answered by a person reading prose.

objects.title: A change whose provenance cannot be reconstructed
objects.description: Attribution stops at the commit, so what authorised a change, what verified it and what governed it are unrecoverable.

objects.title: Finished work that never reached the trunk
objects.description: Workers produce far more than integration absorbs, and nothing distinguishes work that is done from work that is done and landed.

objects.title: debugging
objects.description: reproduce, isolate, fix, and prove a defect fixed

objects.title: deep-work
objects.description: design, architecture, cross-cutting change, or a problem with no known shape

objects.title: implementation
objects.description: build a described feature or change within a known design

objects.title: routine
objects.description: small, well-understood changes; rename, bump, wording, one-line fixes

objects.title: continue
objects.description: resume a task from durable state instead of from someone's memory

objects.title: debug
objects.description: frame a defect so that the fix is proven, not asserted

objects.title: handover
objects.description: produce a continuation record body for the current task

objects.title: review
objects.description: review the working diff against the claimed scope and the finish contract

objects.title: Architecture decision integrity
objects.description: Every architecture decision the repository holds parses against the decision contract, claims an identity nothing else claims, and every relation and reference it makes resolves.

objects.title: AI layer integrity
objects.description: The repository's AI layer is real: the manifest declares a format this executable reads and every section it names exists, the checkout-local half is ignored by git and nothing under it is tracked, and no project data remains under the pre-.ai .majordomus/ path.

objects.title: Blocker resolution
objects.description: No task can be completed while any question on this branch is unresolved; it can still be finished as blocked, partial, no_match or failed.

objects.title: Bootstrap integrity
objects.description: The path from a human reader to the AI layer is unbroken — README.md names AGENTS.md, every generated instruction file points at .ai/README.md, and none of them carries a rule of its own.

objects.title: Catalogue integrity
objects.description: Every use case and application describes the tool in terms the tool has — each command, doctrine and claim it names exists, and the two catalogues reference each other in both directions.

objects.title: Checkpoint freshness
objects.description: A task whose last checkpoint is older than its profile's interval is reported, not stopped.

objects.title: Every public command is exercised and refuted
objects.description: Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed from the registry and the coverage each case declares about itself rather than from a list someone maintains.

objects.title: The command surface is declared and reconciled
objects.description: Every command the binary dispatches is described by the shipped registry, every command the registry declares public is dispatched, and a command is public exactly when the usage text lists it.

objects.title: Completion is gated
objects.description: A task reaches the outcome completed only when no validation gate its own change set selects is known to be failing, and a gate's verdict discharges nothing once the files that select it have changed since the run.

objects.title: Context budget
objects.description: The always-loaded projection stays within its line budget, every reference in it resolves, it states no count that will go stale, and the assembled context fits the builder's own budget.

objects.title: Context integrity
objects.description: Every directory of the AI layer carries a context document, each one carries the contract, they compose into one deterministic chain for every path, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing.

objects.title: Dependency graph integrity
objects.description: The issue dependency graph is acyclic, every edge names an issue that exists, and no issue is executing ahead of a dependency that is not done.

objects.title: Decision records
objects.description: Every entry in decisions.md carries the task, the head and the reason, so a decision can be found by the worker who needs it.

objects.title: The decision threshold
