objects.description: A change that is hard to reverse records the decision behind it as a decision record, and names what it put in force; an ordinary change does not.

objects.title: Define done before executing
objects.description: The finish contract is evaluated line by line, and nothing else counts as done.

objects.title: A deployment is described once, and every provider artifact is generated from it
objects.description: A deployment of the executable is a canonical object of the layer against a closed contract; the container definition and the provider configuration are projections of it, never a second description.

objects.title: Execution depth is not output verbosity
objects.description: Think as hard as the task needs; report as briefly as the profile says.

objects.title: Doctrine wiring integrity
objects.description: Every doctrine in this registry resolves to a validator that exists, is reached from every command it names, propagates failure, is proved by a test, and is run by CI — and every validator in the source is declared here.

objects.title: Enforcement wiring
objects.description: Every enforcement the policy declares is invoked by the hook it names, from a file the dispatcher will actually execute, without swallowing the exit code.

objects.title: Externalise decisions and durable state
objects.description: A decision you make goes into a record, dated, with what was rejected and why; a question for a person goes into the questions store.

objects.title: Handover integrity
objects.description: The resolver runs and reports either the record for this worktree and branch or its clean absence; a malformed record is never silently skipped, and a record describing a history this checkout no longer has is reported.

objects.title: Handovers transfer state, not transcripts
objects.description: A handover says what is true now and the one next action; never conversation history.

objects.title: Parallel work requires isolation
objects.description: Do not start a second task in a checkout that already has one; overlapping claims across worktrees are reported.

objects.title: Escalate capability and effort only when justified
objects.description: The profile sets the default capability and effort; escalation is recorded, never assumed.

objects.title: Layout integrity
objects.description: The directories the durable commands write into are installed rather than created on first use.

objects.title: Ledger integrity
objects.description: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event; the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct stays readable.

objects.title: Lifecycle observation
objects.description: A store that can be read is not a store that is being written. While episodes go on opening, the records a future worker resumes from must go on advancing, every lifecycle event received must leave evidence it arrived, and an episode that outlives the staleness threshold must be named rather than left open.

objects.title: Load minimum sufficient context
objects.description: The profile says what to load; discover everything that may apply and load only what does.

objects.title: Note integrity
objects.description: Every outcome needs a note carrying the sections that outcome requires, and no transcript.

objects.title: Obligation closure
objects.description: A task that declares obligations reaches the outcome completed only when each one is established by the tool or has evidence, and that evidence still describes the tree or the commit it was taken over.

objects.title: One worker, one clear scope
objects.description: A task claims the paths it may touch, and touches only those.

objects.title: Policy completeness
objects.description: Every policy value the code reads is declared in the skeleton policy, and no reader carries its own default for one.

objects.title: Policy integrity
objects.description: The policy and every profile parse, declare version 1, and carry no key the schema does not define.

objects.title: Profile requirements
objects.description: A profile may demand more than the shared contract — a regression test, a decision record — and finish refuses without it.

objects.title: Project model integrity
objects.description: Every milestone and issue file parses, carries the id its filename claims, and contains no key nobody reads.

objects.title: Projection integrity
objects.description: Every generated instruction file exists, matches the stamp it carries, and is never silently overwritten after a hand edit.

objects.title: Prompt capture is proven, or reported unavailable
objects.description: A repository that declares prompt capture has it wired below the model and proven by running it; the archive stays ignored and untracked, every prompt is present as both a record and a rendering, and neither carries anything the model said.

objects.title: A prompt record carries its own identity, is bounded, and is private
objects.description: Every captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or says why it cannot; the archive is readable by its owner alone, bounded by a declared retention policy, and never holds credential material verbatim.

objects.title: Prompt integrity
objects.description: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and every token in it is one the renderer knows.

objects.title: A session does not finish behind its own published site
objects.description: A repository that publishes has a second tree — the one the public is being served — and no commit-level gate can measure it, because no change to any file can make it right or wrong. A session that lands work and leaves the publication owed has finished nothing the public can see, and every check stays green while that is true. The gates that measure a deployment are declared as such in the CI model, and finish asks them.

objects.title: Questions store integrity
objects.description: Every entry in open-questions.md parses, because a gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one.

objects.title: A record's changed_files names the work, not the tool's exhaust
objects.description: The changed_files block of a checkpoint, a handover or a closed session names what the episode produced. Paths a declaration already calls generated, projected or local are classified out, and the classification reads those declarations rather than a list of its own.

objects.title: Retention caps
objects.description: The ledger and the handover directory stay under the caps the policy sets, so durable state does not grow without bound.

objects.title: The roadmap is a projection, never a document
objects.description: No document is a second authority for the roadmap. While a hand-written roadmap table exists, it can neither list a version no milestone declares nor hide one the model does.

objects.title: Rule package integrity
objects.description: The repository's effective rule set is real: the vendored baseline matches its manifest file for file, every rule resolves with its dependencies and no two claim one identity, and no project rule reuses the vendored namespace.

objects.title: Every object has a schema, and the rules resolve in one stated order
objects.description: The order the rules apply in is written down rather than left in the code; every kind the tool reads declares a schema, every schema is named by a kind, and every path under the repository's AI layer is claimed by a source so that nothing is carried through unvalidated.

objects.title: Scope integrity
objects.description: A task touches only the paths it claimed; work found elsewhere is not accepted as done.

objects.title: The episode boundary is drawn below the model, and its working context is local
objects.description: Where a provider fires session events, the episode is opened and closed by that provider's hook rather than by the model, the start event hands the worker the bounded briefing the policy declares, and the working context each open freezes stays under the ignored half of the layer, carries the declared keys, and never carries a conversation.

objects.title: Session records are shared objects with a closed field set
objects.description: A closed execution episode is written once, into the layer's sessions section, against a schema that admits what the repository can prove and nothing else.

objects.title: Sessions are workers, not memory
objects.description: Durable state lives in records the repository keeps, never in a conversation.

objects.title: Skill integrity
objects.description: Every skill the repository declares parses against the skill contract, names the directory it lives in, carries its sections, describes itself in terms no other skill uses, and every skill or example it refers to exists.

objects.title: State consistency
objects.description: The task record still describes this checkout — same branch, and HEAD at or ahead of the recorded commit.

objects.title: Task continuity
objects.description: A task finished as partial or blocked should leave a handover record, not only a note section.

objects.title: Use-case coverage
objects.description: Every public command, and every guaranteed claim and MCP tool the policy asks for, is named and run by at least one active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; a gap is a failure or a report according to the policy, never silence.

objects.title: Verification integrity
objects.description: Completion requires a verification command that actually ran and exited 0; its exit code and duration are recorded.

objects.title: Verify outcomes, not activity
objects.description: A test that ran and passed is evidence; a sentence saying it did is not.

objects.title: An architectural relationship in a published document is drawn, never typed in box art
objects.description: A diagram made of box-drawing characters is a picture nothing can read — it cannot be rendered, linked, themed or checked against what it claims to describe, and on a phone it is the one element that cannot wrap. Every architectural relationship a published document states is a mermaid block; literal terminal output, file listings and quoted file content are not diagrams and are exempt by declaration.

objects.title: A generator that cannot match the tree refuses rather than rewriting it
objects.description: An executable asked to generate this repository's derived artifacts first establishes that it was built from the same declarations the tree carries; when it cannot, it refuses and says so, because a generator that guesses rewrites the documents it was meant to check.

objects.title: A verdict states what it is a verdict about
objects.description: A check reports the size and the identity of the population it examined, never a bare count or an "every one" whose denominator is elsewhere; and a detector that greps for a literal may not count its own prose, its own fixtures or another language's builtin as its subject.

objects.title: A worker that stops leaves its work where somebody else can find it
objects.description: Work that exists only in one worker's working tree is invisible to every other and dies with the worker; anyone who fans work out is responsible for checkpointing it, because a worker's death is not a rollback.

objects.title: Everything that accumulates is measured, bounded and reaped by a committed command
objects.description: Open pull requests, linked worktrees, local branches, running servers and the disk their build output holds all grow on their own and none of them shrinks on its own; each is measured by one committed command, carries a threshold that makes growth loud, and is reduced by a command that is safe to run unattended — never by a name match against a process list, never by deleting a worktree whose work is not published, and never by a predicate whose missing input becomes a verdict.

objects.title: Every public command is benchmarkable from the registry
objects.description: The benchmark targets are the public commands of share/commands.yaml and their scenarios are the command fixtures; no second list of what to time exists, and a command whose fixture the harness cannot run is a defect of the fixture, not an exemption.

objects.title: Blocking checks are deterministic and cheap
objects.description: A check that can stop a command is deterministic and cheap; work in progress is reported, never blocked.

objects.title: A cache never changes what a command observes
objects.description: A cache of derived state, if one exists, is keyed by the version of the canonical state it derives from, is bypassable, and produces byte-identical output to the uncached path; a cache that can be observed through a command's output, exit code or findings is a defect, and a cache that no case proves equivalent does not exist.

objects.title: A collection has one order, owned by one place, and it does not depend on who ran the command
objects.description: Every collection this repository shows a person or a stable machine consumer is ordered by apps/majordomus-cli/src/order.rs — a total order over group, explicit rank, natural label and canonical identity — and no consumer holds an ordering opinion of its own; a comparator that folds case by hand, a sort key that renders markup, and a comparison that collates by the reader's locale are all refused.

objects.title: Clean room
objects.description: The Prismatic name is the only thing carried from anywhere else: no internal paths, hostnames, component names, doctrine vocabulary or quotations.

objects.title: A command is declared once, and every surface that shows it is a projection
objects.description: Every command this repository offers is declared in the program that implements it and nowhere else; the workflow runner, the shell completion, the machine surfaces, the Cockpit and the documentation are projections of one composed graph, so adding a command requires no second registration and no surface can carry a command catalogue that goes stale.

objects.title: A command runs with nobody at the keyboard
objects.description: Where a non-interactive form of a command exists it is the one used — pagers disabled, confirmations passed as flags, stdin supplied explicitly — so that no step of any automated run can block waiting for a person who is not there.

objects.title: Completion is proved by one policy, derived from evidence, and never claimed
objects.description: The definition of done is one shipped declaration, share/completion.yaml, whose every question names the source its answer is taken from. The completion report derives the lifecycle stage a task stands at and the one bit `complete` from those answers, every surface reads that report, and the outcome completed is refused while the bit is false. A state a worker sets, a checklist a worker ticks, or a second list of what done means anywhere is the defect.

objects.title: Context locality
objects.description: Context lives in the narrowest directory scope where it stays correct; root files bootstrap and link, provider files are projections.

objects.title: Conventional commits, committed and pushed incrementally
objects.description: Commits use the conventional format type(scope): description with the co-author footer the session provides, and land incrementally rather than as one large change.

objects.title: A deployment is verified by asking the deployed surface what it serves
objects.description: Every surface a change reaches — the published site, the published release metadata, each active deployment object — is asked for the identity it states at its own address and compared with the revision the trunk expects. A surface stating an older identity is stale, one that does not answer is unreachable, a reachable one with no identity is unreadable, and none of those is a pass. Which surfaces a change reaches is derived from what the repository declares, never from a list of deploy commands, and a target that does not apply is in the plan with the reason.

objects.title: Derived files are regenerated, never edited
objects.description: A generated file is changed by changing its canonical source and rerunning the generator, and both are committed together; a commit that leaves the derived data behind its inputs is refused before it exists.

objects.title: Derived state is computed once per state version
objects.description: Anything derivable solely from unchanged canonical repository state is computed once per version of that state and read many times; a command's hot path does not rediscover, reparse or rebuild it per item, per request or per call.

objects.title: The design is one typed declaration and every first-party surface consumes its projections
objects.description: Roles, status semantics, type scale, layout, radius, motion, theme contract and brand are declared once in share/design/tokens.yaml, read by the crate as a typed model, and projected by `majordomus generate design` into the stylesheets both Tailwind builds import, the tokens and declaration compiled into the executable, every copy of the brand, the site's dataset and the reference; a first-party surface names a token and never chooses a value, a state word is coloured by the meaning it is filed under, and a token added to the declaration reaches every surface with no consumer edited.

objects.title: A sweep that deletes fails closed on what it could not read
objects.description: Any script that selects paths for deletion by a measured predicate — age, size, staleness — treats a predicate input it could not read as false, never as an extreme value; it names what it is about to delete and the measurement behind the verdict before deleting, and it reports how many candidates it skipped for want of a readable input.

objects.title: Development semantics live in the canonical runtime; a surface only consumes them
objects.description: A semantic of the development lifecycle — the plan, tasks, sessions, context, executions, peers, evidence, obligations and completion — is declared once as a capability of the Rust executable's registry, and the Cockpit, the CLI, the HTTP API, OpenAPI and MCP request it rather than deciding it; a surface that computes a status, decides a transition or writes a development object itself is a second implementation and a defect.

objects.title: A return code is not the diagnostic channel
objects.description: A command that emits an error diagnostic does not exit zero; every derivation and every check runs so that an error in the layer stops it.

objects.title: Distribution has one canonical model
objects.description: Supported targets, artifact names, installer resolution, the release build matrix, the documentation, the website and the exposed API metadata are derived from share/distribution.yaml or mechanically validated against it; none of them states a platform, a name or an installation URL of its own.

objects.title: An empty result and a failed command must not look alike
objects.description: A command that could not answer is reported as a command that could not answer, never as a command that answered nothing; a caller that cannot tell the two apart acts on a confident wrong answer.

objects.title: English only
objects.description: Code, comments, commits, documents and governance records are written in English, with no exceptions.

objects.title: Entering the repository converges on a server, by either door, without anything to remember
objects.description: An agent entering the repository is owed a ready shared server before its first attach and gets one through the provider's start event; a shell entering the repository is owed the same and gets it through one bootstrap command of the executable, which the entry file calls and nothing else; neither entry path builds the executable, ensures from a stale one, waits for readiness or fails; what a worker is told on entry is derived from the same typed reading every other surface uses; entry has a declared time budget; and a server no client owns ends by itself.

objects.title: The shell entry point is an adapter, and it makes one call
objects.description: A file a shell evaluates on entering the repository resolves the tool and makes exactly one call to it — the bootstrap command — evaluating what that call exports; it reads nothing about the repository itself, builds nothing, and reaches no network of its own, so that entering a directory cannot be slow, cannot fail, and cannot become a second implementation of what the executable already knows.

objects.title: Every wait is bounded
objects.description: Every wait carries a timeout, a completion predicate and a recovery path; nothing is spawned without a condition that decides when it is done, and an absence of output is inspected rather than read as progress.

objects.title: A long operation reports typed events, and a transport only renders them
objects.description: An operation long enough to be watched reports its steps, its progress and its findings as typed execution events produced by the domain and published to one store; the WebSocket, the HTTP history route, the command line and the Cockpit render that value and contain no execution logic, and the schema every client validates against is derived from the Rust types rather than written down.

objects.title: Execution state is authoritative and the terminal is not
objects.description: A worker decides whether to continue from execution state — exit status, structured output, state artifacts, messages, logs — and never from terminal focus, keystrokes or renderer activity; a finished delegate's result is consumed when it is ready, not when somebody looks at the pane.

objects.title: A sensitive value never enters an execution
objects.description: A value an input schema marks sensitive is replaced once, before the input is stored, so that no execution snapshot, event, history, log, page, listing or generated document can carry it; what a schema marks is the only rule, and a field's name is never one.

objects.title: Every finding carries a reproduce command
objects.description: Every finding a command reports names the command that reproduces it.

objects.title: A generated artifact declares its document, its encoding, its contract and its source
objects.description: Every file the generator writes declares the document it projects, the encoding it is written in, the JSON Schema its content satisfies and where it came from; it carries a provenance header in the form that encoding allows; a structured document is written in every encoding this repository commits it in from one value; and the manifest of the whole set is itself generated.

objects.title: The GitHub projection is checked by a gate, not by somebody remembering to run it
objects.description: A projection this repository claims is generated from the canonical model is proved by a gate that reads the remote and fails on drift; a detector that exists but is never called is not enforcement, and a gate that cannot reach the remote reports that it cannot rather than passing.

objects.title: A command reads each canonical file at most once
objects.description: Within one invocation a command flattens, hashes or parses a canonical file at most once, however many validators, accessors or projections need it; the second reader gets the first reading.

objects.title: External interfaces are projections of one capability definition
objects.description: A capability is defined once, as a typed descriptor in Rust or as a declarative object with its schema in the layer, and MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI, CLI introspection and the generated reference are derived from it.

objects.title: Work lands often and small, and what is published is master and only master
objects.description: A branch merges to master as soon as it is green rather than waiting for a batch; master is merged into it locally first, so the derived merge driver resolves what GitHub cannot; the published site is built from master alone; the commit gh-pages names is an ancestor of master; and the person who merged is the person who checks that it reached the public.

objects.title: The mesh observes nodes; it authorizes nothing and holds one registry
objects.description: Mesh discovery is provider-based, signed and canonical — providers emit observations into the one MeshRegistry through the manager's single verification path, no discovery event grants execution or trust by presence, and the mesh is off until a repository declares it.

objects.title: A native command line command exists only with its documentation and its executable examples
objects.description: Every command of the Rust executable is declared once in clap with the examples beside it, every command a person can run carries at least one example that the crate's tests execute against the built binary, and the generated reference, the site dataset and the routes under /docs/cli/ are projections that CI refuses to let go stale.

objects.title: The site's navigation is declared once, and every projection derives from that declaration
objects.description: site/data/nav.toml is the one statement of what the site's navigation is — its groups, their items and the single call to action. Every surface that shows a route a visitor navigates to renders that file; no href is written twice in it, the primary navigation stays small enough to be a set of questions rather than a sitemap, and no template types a site route beside the declaration.

objects.title: Never author identity fields
objects.description: repository_id, branch, head, working_tree and changed_files on any record are computed from git and never written by hand.

objects.title: A verdict that never arrived is not a verdict
objects.description: A change is judged against the trunk's own failing set, established by reading a run that finished, and never against the absence of a report; a check that has not spoken is unknown, not passing.

objects.title: Never store or summarise transcripts
objects.description: No record stores or summarises a conversation; records carry what is true now and the next action.

objects.title: New and changed executable code is covered by a test; legacy debt may only shrink
objects.description: Every executable line, function and region a change adds or touches in the Rust crate must be covered by a test, measured over the same export and test-exclusion as the crate gate; untouched legacy debt is out of scope, and no change may add debt.

objects.title: No claim without a test
objects.description: A capability sentence in README.md or docs/ is backed by a case in test/cases/ or is phrased as a target.

objects.title: No counts in prose
objects.description: Prose never states a number the repository can compute; it states the command that computes it.

objects.title: Nothing this repository commits names a path of the machine it was written on
objects.description: No committed file records an absolute path of somebody's home directory or working copy, whether a person wrote it or the generator did; a path a generated artifact records is repository-relative, and the helper that computes one is defined once in the crate.

objects.title: No network, no telemetry, no eval, no silent overwrite, no recursive deletion
objects.description: bin/, lib/, share/ and test/ contain no telemetry, no eval, no curl piped to a shell, no silent overwrite, no recursive deletion outside a temporary directory, and no network client but the one declared exception SECURITY.md names.

objects.title: No new nouns
objects.description: The tool gains no agents, personas, roles, tiers or registries beyond the vocabulary it has.

objects.title: A command is the projection of a capability, or it says why it is not, and the reason is checked
objects.description: Every runnable command of the native command line is bound to a canonical capability, or classified in one typed place with a structural reason that the parity check verifies; a command in neither place is a finding, and so is a classification that has gone stale.

objects.title: Complexity is optional, not ambient
objects.description: Simple things are trivial, complex things possible, weird things hackable; a change that makes the default path harder, adds a foundational noun without a concrete need, or leaks internals into ordinary use is refused in review.

objects.title: A performance claim carries its measurement
objects.description: A change made for speed names the phase or counter it changed and both values, measured on this repository with the tool's own timing; a budget or a threshold is set from a run, never guessed; a baseline is a tracked file written by the harness and updated on purpose.

objects.title: Portable shell
objects.description: bash 3.2 and BSD userland are the floor: no associative arrays, no mapfile, no GNU-only flags, and shellcheck -x -s bash passes on every script.

objects.title: What the product does is a catalogue object, and every public surface of it is derived
objects.description: Every product feature is one schema-valid file under the layer's features section, holding references and editorial decisions only; the interfaces, counts, links, moments and routes every surface shows are derived from those references, and a page, template, generator or navigation file that names a feature, module, command, provider or count by hand is a defect.

objects.title: What a provider's adapter can do is declared, never observed from the filesystem
objects.description: The lifecycle events a provider's adapter drives, and whether it can archive prompts, are declared in share/providers.yaml and read there by every surface; no reader answers the question by looking for an installed hook, and no document carries its own list.

objects.title: What the tool knows about a provider is declared once and projected everywhere
objects.description: A provider's title, the client configuration it reads and the scratch roots it creates checkouts under are declared in share/providers.yaml beside its template and nowhere else; the table a person reads is docs/generated/providers.md, generated from the same value the product, the site and the worktree topology answer from; no document enumerates providers by hand.

objects.title: A worker reclaims only what it owns
objects.description: Build output, scratch trees and worktrees belong to whoever is working in them; a worker under disk pressure reclaims its own and says what it removed, because everything else on the machine is another worker's instrument.

objects.title: Recovery looks before it repeats
objects.description: Before retrying interrupted work a worker establishes what already happened — artifacts on disk, git state, test and build output, task records — and resumes from there; recovery never duplicates a commit, a file, a migration or any other side effect.

objects.title: The changelog is composed and the version has one writer
objects.description: What this project has shipped is derived from the layer's own release records, the decisions dated inside each release's window and the commits in its range, so no changelog is kept by hand; the version is stated in the two sites that must state it and raised by one command that writes both, so the two never drift apart by an edit somebody forgot to make twice.

objects.title: A new enforced rule is a doctrine, not an inline check
objects.description: A rule the tool enforces declares an x-majordomus block — a validator named mj_validate_<name> when a command runs it, the tests that prove it when a gate does; no command selects checks by hand.

objects.title: No endpoint of the Rust executable without a benchmark, and no number without evidence
objects.description: Every externally callable operation of the Rust executable (each executable capability directly and on every transport its exposure declares, and the transports' own operations) is a benchmark target with a denominator generated from the registry; coverage is complete or the structural check fails; a waiver is typed, reported and never counted; and a claim about latency is made from a recorded measurement, never from prose.

objects.title: One canonical declaration; modules compose capabilities; the root composes modules
objects.description: An executable capability of the Rust executable is declared once with capability!, composed into its module with module!, and the application composes modules with compose_modules!; every interface, benchmark target, cache behaviour and generated document is derived from that declaration, and editing a projection to add or change one is a defect.

objects.title: The Rust executable carries its evidence with it
objects.description: Every capability and every documented behaviour of apps/majordomus-cli is proved by a behavioural test, every public item is documented with an executable example where one is meaningful, line coverage stays above the threshold CI enforces, and the hot paths carry benchmarks.

objects.title: A command asserts in the file that declares it that it is what it claims, and is composed rather than registered
objects.description: Every capability module the executable composes carries at least one assertion that runs beside the declaration — an in-file test or an executed doc example — is reached by the root composition rather than by a registration elsewhere, and is held to a declared coverage floor.

objects.title: A request never rebuilds canonical state, and a cache is never trusted without an equivalence test
objects.description: After the Rust executable has started, no MCP or HTTP request scans the repository, builds the index or the registry, derives a schema or builds a projection; every call goes through the one executor; a cache exists only where a measurement justified it, is bounded, is keyed by the registry fingerprint, and is proved to answer what the handler answers.

objects.title: Every exported Rust item explains itself, shows itself running, and is exercised by something
objects.description: The crate's exported surface is measured from its own syntax tree — documentation that says more than the signature, an executable example on everything that carries behaviour, and a module boundary that something exercises — and what the policy does not ask for is derived and printed rather than exempted by a list.

objects.title: What a worker reads is declared once, and nothing outside it is read or served
objects.description: The repository scope, the pathspecs a worker reads and the paths, names, sizes and content it never reads, is declared once as data in .ai/repo/scope.yaml (or the distribution's default when a repository declares none), and the Rust executable discovers, indexes and serves nothing outside it, answers for any path whether it is in or out and why, and reports a tracked secret.

objects.title: Nothing a client leaves behind locks another client out
objects.description: The shared MCP server is a client's child; whatever state a client or a dead server leaves behind is taken over or bypassed, and a client that cannot share is served alone, never turned away.

objects.title: Tests run in disposable repositories
objects.description: Behavioural cases run through bash test/run.sh in a temporary repository each, never against this checkout.

objects.title: The briefing an episode opened with is compared against git before it is believed
objects.description: The working context a provider's start hook freezes is a recorded head like every other, so the surfaces that hand it to a worker label it against the current checkout in the vocabulary the rest of the repository already uses, and none of them refuses an episode for having drifted.

objects.title: The shared server's lease has one reader
objects.description: The file that says which process serves a checkout and at which address is parsed by one typed reader in the executable and served from there; no other file in this repository opens it, and a caller that needs the address asks `serve status`.

objects.title: A long-lived process serves the repository as it is, never as it was when it started
objects.description: The shared server follows the repository it serves; a commit made while it runs is visible through every surface it offers, without a restart and without a poll.

objects.title: The version is measured against the public surface, not claimed
objects.description: What a release's version number says about compatibility is decided by one typed engine comparing the capability registry of the last release with this tree — identities, bindings and both schemas of each capability — and a version smaller than what moved is refused, by the writer as well as by the gate. Commit subjects are evidence beside that verdict and never the authority for it. Below 1.0.0 the floor is a minor release and a removal is named rather than refused; at 1.0.0 the shift ends.

objects.title: AI client instructions are derived from canonical repository metadata, never maintained by hand
objects.description: The instruction file each AI client reads — AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, every projection the policy declares — is generated from the policy and the shipped declarations, stamped with the hash of what produced it, and refused when edited by hand or when its source has moved. What the files say about the lifecycle, and in particular the definition of done, is a fragment rendered from share/completion.yaml by both renderers to the same bytes. A capability inventory, a command list or a lifecycle stated in a client file by hand is the defect; policy changes by changing the source and regenerating, never by editing a projection.

objects.title: Every page of every web surface is audited, and the audit names no page
objects.description: The user interface is held to one executable standard — responsive at every width the theme declares, keyboard-operable, and WCAG 2.1 AA — over a page set and a width set that are discovered rather than listed.

objects.title: Unknown configuration keys are errors
objects.description: Every configuration file rejects a key nothing reads, and every state field is both written and read.

objects.title: A use case is proved by execution, and a capability is covered by a use case
objects.description: Every externally meaningful capability of this repository is demonstrated by an active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; every example a page shows comes from that execution; a use case's maturity is observed, never authored; and a change to a command, rule, claim, provider, MCP tool, schema, application or workflow runs use-case impact analysis before the work is called complete.

objects.title: A web surface is declared once and every web projection is derived from it
objects.description: Everything this repository exposes over HTTP is one resolved surface with a mount, a producer and provenance; the router, the landing page, the machine-readable index, the published tree, the generated reference and the benchmark targets are projections of that resolution, and no second list of routes exists anywhere.

objects.title: A web surface is discovered from its producer, never registered twice
objects.description: Everything this repository exposes over HTTP is one resolved topology, discovered from producers and projected to serving, publication, validation and documentation from that one resolution.

objects.title: An operational failure mode is a catalogue object, never a page
objects.description: Every user-visible operational problem this tool answers is one schema-valid file under the layer's why section, and every listing, route, filter, count, backlink, API answer and diagnosis is derived from it; a projection that registers one is a defect.

objects.title: What already claims a path is checked before that path is built
objects.description: Before implementing something that creates a new module, command group, document kind or generated artifact, a worker asks what already claims those paths across every local and remote branch (scripts/collision-check --new <paths>), not only who the peer board says is working now, and announces its own intent afterwards.

objects.title: A branch's worktree is at <repo>-wt/<branch>, derived from git, never registered
objects.description: Every non-trunk branch that is worked on has exactly one linked worktree, at the primary checkout's sibling container `<repo>-wt` under the branch's own name with its hierarchy kept; the primary checkout hosts the trunk; the path is derived from git identity by the executable's worktree service and recorded nowhere; a worktree somewhere else is a typed diagnostic that only an explicit, fingerprint-verified migration repairs, and no repair ever destroys uncommitted work.

objects.title: Repository review
objects.description: An evidence-driven review of the actual state of the repository, or of one change to it, before meaningful engineering work is recommended or done.

objects.title: Getting started and adoption
objects.description: Bringing Majordomus into a repository, new or old, without losing what people already wrote.

objects.title: Completion and quality gates
objects.description: Deciding whether work is finished, with a contract every line of which passes or fails.

objects.title: Sessions and handover
objects.description: Stopping and resuming work across sessions and workers from durable state, never a transcript.

objects.title: Drift and reconciliation
objects.description: Detecting that policy, projections, state and git disagree, and putting them back in step.

objects.title: Extension
objects.description: Adding a kind, a rule, a command or a use case as data, with the checks that follow from it.

objects.title: Repository knowledge
objects.description: What the repository declares about itself: sources, nodes, edges, the plan, and searching them.

objects.title: Serving the layer to AI clients
objects.description: One shared server per repository, every client a peer, the same layer over MCP, HTTP and the command line.

objects.title: Performance
objects.description: Benchmarks derived from the registry, baselines that are data, and budgets doctor reports against.

objects.title: Policy and enforcement
objects.description: Declaring rules, proving they are wired, and reproducing a finding.

objects.title: Parallel workers
objects.description: Several agents or people on one repository: claimed scopes, overlap, and who touched what.

objects.title: Decide whether finished work is actually finished
objects.description: Evaluate a contract line by line instead of accepting a sentence that says the work is done.

objects.title: Add a use case and let the tool prove it
objects.description: Scaffold a draft for an uncovered command, validate it, run its scenario against the real tool, and see the coverage move.

objects.title: Adopt a repository that already has its own rules
objects.description: Install the supervisory layer into a repository with a hand-written CLAUDE.md, without the tool taking ownership of a file somebody else wrote.

objects.title: Block acceptance on a question nobody has answered
objects.description: Open a question against the task, watch finish refuse completion while it is unresolved, resolve it with the answer, and only then complete.

objects.title: Keep the prompts that started the work, below the model rather than around it
objects.description: Wire the provider hook, prove it by running a payload through it, and see that a prompt the tool could not parse is reported rather than silently dropped.

objects.title: Hand work over with a question still open, and keep it blocking
objects.description: Close a task into a handover while a question is unresolved, start the follow-up task, and see the same question still refuse acceptance there.

objects.title: Checkpoint long work so a stop costs minutes, not the day
objects.description: Record compact progress inside the active task at the profile interval, so a session that ends without warning leaves the next one a place to start.

objects.title: Decide what belongs in the AI context, as data
objects.description: Read the repository’s declared scope policy, see which paths are in and out of the index, and let doctor and the knowledge index apply it rather than a hardcoded list.

objects.title: Complete an issue only when its evidence exists
objects.description: See an issue refuse completion while a required piece of evidence is missing, read the roadmap the milestone state derives, and keep the GitHub projection a projection.

objects.title: Deliver issues in waves the graph computes, and take the next one
objects.description: Validate the plan, read the execution waves the dependency graph yields, see which issues are ready and which are blocked on what, and take the one issue a worker should do now.

objects.title: Refuse a directory of the layer that documents nothing
objects.description: A directory added under the layer without a context document fails validation by name, nothing resolves against the tree until it says what it is for, and the same hierarchy is readable over MCP and the API without running the gate.

objects.title: Extend what the executable serves by adding a file, never by rebuilding it
objects.description: Add a rule, a prompt or a knowledge node to .ai/ and have it appear as an MCP resource, an HTTP route and a reference entry, with the same binary.

objects.title: Find an object of the layer without reading everything
objects.description: Search durable records literally across kinds from the shell, and ask the shared server the same question over MCP with majordomus_search and majordomus_get.

objects.title: Find out what has drifted since anyone last looked
objects.description: Ask what has moved, rather than whether anything is wrong.

objects.title: Follow a procedure the repository defines, and add another one
objects.description: Read the repository''s skills, take one as it is written, and add a new one by writing its file — no registry, no code, and a check that says what it examined.

objects.title: Gate CI on the tool itself, with an exit code that is a contract
objects.description: Run the checks CI runs, read every finding with the command that reproduces it, and rely on exit codes that mean one thing each: no code means warn and continue.

objects.title: Hand the repository to someone who cannot clone it
objects.description: Take a snapshot that a model can read or a gate can run in, without sending anything untracked and without losing the file modes on the way.

objects.title: Hand unfinished work to the next session
objects.description: Stop mid-task and leave the next worker something to act on that is not a transcript.

objects.title: Install the tool in one command, on a machine with no toolchain
objects.description: Paste one line, get a verified binary for this machine, and run majordomus init — no git, no Rust, no Node, no Python, no root, and no way to install an archive whose digest does not match.

objects.title: Record a decision so the next worker can find it
objects.description: Write down what was decided and why as state, then find it again without reading a conversation.

objects.title: Keep every provider bootstrap thin, generated and within budget
objects.description: Regenerate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the other provider files from one policy and prove they are stamped, point at the layer, stay under the line budget and resolve every reference.

objects.title: Know whether the work in this checkout is finished
objects.description: Ask the repository you are standing in, and be told what is still owed by name.

objects.title: Check the version before trusting a diagnosis
objects.description: Print the version every other surface derives from, and see the argument it refuses.

objects.title: Have the session opened and closed without anybody remembering to
objects.description: Wire the provider''s own session events, and the episode opens when the sitting begins, hands the worker what the last one left, records what a compaction is about to discard, and closes with a continuation record beside its envelope.

objects.title: Move a repository from the pre-.ai layout to the layer
objects.description: See what a migration would move, move it with a backup, and prove the result is a layer the tool reads.

objects.title: Record what one worker did in one sitting
objects.description: Open a session, do the work under whatever tasks it touches, and close it into an envelope that references what it produced and copies nothing.

objects.title: Keep the plan as milestones and issues the tool can validate
objects.description: Declare milestones as outcomes and issues as execution contracts, and let the tool say what is ready and what is blocked.

objects.title: Prove a rule is actually enforced, not merely written down
objects.description: Answer "is this rule real?" with a command rather than a reading of the source.

objects.title: Prove the tool is fast, not assume it, and refuse a regression
objects.description: Measure every public command and every capability of the executable against a committed baseline, and let the check fail on a regression rather than a reviewer noticing later.

objects.title: Prove what a task owed before calling it done
objects.description: A task declares what it owes, records evidence against each obligation, and is refused when that evidence no longer describes the tree it was taken over.

objects.title: Read back what happened, and keep the ledger within its cap
objects.description: Read the append-only ledger as operational history, filtered by task and event, validate every line, and rotate the oldest lines into an archive rather than deleting them.

objects.title: Read only the context that fits the budget, and know what was dropped
objects.description: Assemble the context a worker needs now in authority order, cut it to a line budget, and see every dropped section named with its reason.

objects.title: See which rules apply here and what enforces them
objects.description: List the effective rule set, read one rule as the tool reads it, and see which of them the tool enforces and from where.

objects.title: Record a decision as data, and prove the tool cannot accept it for you
objects.description: Read the decisions a repository holds, validate the whole set in one command, and watch the tool refuse to write the one status only a person may write.

objects.title: Close an episode whose client never came back
objects.description: A killed provider sends no end event. Close the episode it left open by evidence, exactly once, without claiming work it did not do.

objects.title: Start a session from a rendered framing, not a pasted transcript
objects.description: List the prompt assets the repository ships, render one against the durable state, and read the context it embeds.

objects.title: Resume in the right worktree, never against somebody else’s task
objects.description: Find the handover that belongs to this worktree and branch, and see a task record from another checkout reported as foreign rather than enforced here.

objects.title: Run several workers in one repository without them colliding
objects.description: Give each worker a declared scope, and find out immediately when two of them claim the same paths.

objects.title: Say what reached the remote and what did not
objects.description: The obligations that reach past the working tree are settled by asking git and the published site, so a report cannot call uncommitted work committed or unpushed work pushed.

objects.title: Say what your work is for, once, and have every surface say it
objects.description: Record an operational failure mode as one file and have the command line, the API, MCP and the website answer it without registering it anywhere.

objects.title: See what the repository holds, and run one of its capabilities, without reading a file
objects.description: Open the shared server in a browser and get the whole layer as pages: what exists, where each thing came from, what depends on what, what is failing, and a form that runs any capability.

objects.title: Serve the repository's AI layer to every AI client through one shared server
objects.description: Open the repository in any client the tool declares a provider for (docs/generated/providers.md) and have each of them read the same rules, prompts and knowledge over MCP from one process, seeing each other.

objects.title: Trace a change to the context documents it affects
objects.description: List the scoped context documents, resolve which apply to a path and why, and find out which documents a change set touches before it lands.

objects.title: Trust the policy and the profiles only after they are validated
objects.description: Prove that the canonical policy parses with every key it needs declared, that every profile parses and the default exists, and that what the policy declares as enforced is what actually runs.

objects.title: Work on a branch in the one worktree it belongs to
objects.description: Start a branch without choosing a path, find every checkout of the repository from any of them, and bring a stray one home with its uncommitted work intact.

objects.title: The Majordomus project in ChatGPT
objects.description: The operator's own ChatGPT Project holding design conversation about this repository, read so that what was decided there can be cited, carried and promoted here.

cli.about: Majordomus control plane: a data-driven MCP server over the repository's .ai/ layer
cli.long_about:
The Rust executable of Majordomus. It reads the repository's provider-neutral AI layer under .ai/ and serves it to MCP clients over stdio. Almost every capability is a query; the few that change anything declare themselves as commands and are listed by `capabilities list --kind command`.

Most of the task lifecycle (init, start, check, finish, doctor, ...) is the shell tool bin/majordomus in the same repository. Development semantics are converging onto capabilities of this registry one at a time (ADR 0040); until one has, this executable does not implement that command.

examples.title: What the contract did, and the smallest version it allows
examples.description: The public capability surface of this tree against the one the last release published, and the smallest version this tree may therefore declare. The compatibility level is measured from the contract rather than read off the commit subjects: a capability, route, MCP tool, command or required field a caller could hold and cannot any more is breaking whatever the commit that removed it called itself. The same value answers `GET /api/v1/release/analysis`, the `majordomus_release_analysis` MCP tool, the Cockpit's Release page and the `version-surface` gate. A repository that has published nothing has no baseline to measure against, and says so with exit 12 rather than reporting an empty diff — which would read as "nothing changed".

examples.description: The one writer, and it computes nothing: it reads the plan `release analyze` prints and applies it, so the version it writes is the measured minimum rather than a judgement of its own. `--level` and `--exact` name a higher version when a person means more than the contract did, and are refused below the minimum with nothing written — an override that could undershoot would make the measurement decorative.
